meaning.levelBasis: outcome: the source assigns this outcome to this level (its code, unit, course configuration, or a single-level course). course: the source assigns no level, so the outcome is listed at every level its course offers.
meaning.units: Only units at this level, or level-less units holding an outcome at this level; outcomeIds keeps only this level's outcomes.
meaning.configurations: Only the course configurations for this level.
meaning.document: Only the document units at this level (all of them for a single-level course).

statusMeaning.imported: Copied automatically from the outcome's official page. Not yet checked by a person.
statusMeaning.cross-checked: Copied automatically from the outcome's official page, and the Ministry's CSV file has the same words in the same order (ignoring punctuation and spacing; the CSV shortens some long statements, and then its words must match the start). Not yet checked by a person.
statusMeaning.document-extracted: A course's `document`: copied from the text layer of the official curriculum document (PDF) by scripts/curriculum/documents/. Not yet checked by a person.
statusMeaning.document-ocr-unverified: A course's `document`: read by OCR from a scanned official curriculum document (PDF) and not proofread. Check every item against the printed page before use.

flagsMeaning.listedInMenu: The site's Browse by Subject or Browse by Grade menus link to the course (otherwise it is reachable only through the search list).
flagsMeaning.legacy: An older curriculum that a renewed one replaces; see legacyEvidence.
flagsMeaning.notACurriculum: A site entry with no curriculum behind it; see notACurriculumEvidence.

outcomes.statement: Evaluate the operation and viability of a merchandising business from an accounting perspective.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 14 : Introduction to Merchandising (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-5 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 11

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Investigate the difference between a service business and a merchandising business.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Analyze local, provincial, national and international examples of merchandising (buying and selling) between producer, manufacturer, wholesaler, retailer and consumer.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Evaluate business decisions related to import/export costs, product sustainability, local vs international merchandise and the impact those decisions have on the financial profits/loss of a business.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify examples of merchandising businesses within the community and examine the viability of the business.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Interview an owner of a merchandising business in the community to discuss operational information.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explain the difference between the acquisition price and the selling price of a product.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Discuss the meaning of markup, margin and markdown.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explain purchases and their related accounts as being the main record of costs of the merchandise for resale in a periodic inventory system.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Design a proposal for a home-based or online merchandising business, including components such as cost price, profit, overhead, selling price, salaries, delivery, advertising, income tax benefits, primary or secondary source revenue, supplier and markdown.

outcomes.statement: Explain the purpose and application of the Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAPs).
outcomes.printedWith: Module 15: Accounting Standards and Business Ethics (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-3 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 2

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss how Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAPs) and accounting standards are applied to accounting cycles and to business transactions.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Collaborate with peers to discuss inquiry questions such as: Why do GAAPs and accounting standards exist? How are the GAAPs applied? What would happen in the absence of any standards?

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Examine the relationship between personal, professional and business ethics and how it relates to GAAPs and the accounting standards.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Discuss why different parts of accounting handbook exist (e.g., International Financial Reporting Standards [IFRS], Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises [ASPE], Not-for-profit organizations [NPO], Public Sector Accounting Board [PSAB]).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Investigate accounting examples of current events that involve a breach in ethics or failure to adhere to accounting standards.

outcomes.statement: Explore the importance of inventory and its accurate value within a merchandising business.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 16: Merchandising Inventory Accounts (Core) · Suggested Time: 4-6 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 14

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Define merchandising inventory.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Classify and assign a number to the different types of accounts used in a merchandising business such as merchandise inventory, purchases, sales and cost of goods sold to the chart of accounts.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Examine the inquiry questions: Why is inventory reported on the balance sheet as the amount paid for the item, not the selling price? Why is the cost of goods sold reported on the income statement?

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Discuss the relationship between beginning inventory (e.g., cost of goods on hand) and ending inventory.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Calculate the balance of merchandise inventory in a merchandising business.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Differentiate between perpetual inventory and periodic inventory, considering cost, ease of handling, computerization and labour hours.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Analyze the implications of inventory surplus or deficits in a business (e.g., cash flow, expenses, loss).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Calculate the cost of goods sold.

outcomes.statement: Assess sales and purchase accounts for a merchandising business.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 17: Sales and Purchases Accounts (Core) · Suggested Time: 9-12 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 16

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Distinguish between cash and purchase transactions.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Analyze sales tax as a liability in a business and how it is calculated on sales transactions.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Assess discounts and how they apply to purchases (e.g., 2/10 n/30 – 2% off if paid within 10 days or net 30) in a merchandising business.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Analyze the effect that sales returns and discounts have on original sales transactions.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Implement contra accounts to record returns and allowances transactions.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Analyze a sales invoice to see if all relevant components including seller, buyer, date, quantity, date, amount, item, tax, terms and total are noted.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Implement the use of special journals (e.g., purchases, cash payments, sales, cash receipts, departmental journals).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Organize transactions into the appropriate sales or purchase journals.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Distinguish between the general ledger and the subsidiary ledgers.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Discuss how the controlling accounts receivable and the controlling accounts payable account summarize all accounts from the subsidiary ledgers.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Produce a schedule of accounts payable and accounts receivable ensuring the total matches the appropriate controlling account.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Post-sales on account transactions, totals, merchandise purchases, cash receipts and cash payments to the appropriate ledger or column.

indicators.label: m
indicators.text: Critique how cash on delivery (COD), on account, charge, discounts and returns all impact the sales revenue of a merchandising business.

indicators.label: n
indicators.text: Explain how sales and related accounts are the main source of revenue in a merchandising business.

indicators.label: o
indicators.text: Classify purchases and related accounts (e.g., source documents, invoice, returns and allowances, discounts) as well as invoice and transportation costs (e.g., freight-in, free on board destination).

indicators.label: p
indicators.text: Explain purchases and its related accounts as being the main record of costs of the merchandise for resale in a periodic inventory system.

indicators.label: q
indicators.text: Apply generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) to sales and purchases.

outcomes.statement: Implement steps 1-3 of the accounting cycle for a merchandising business.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 18: Steps 1-3 of Accounting cycle for Merchandising Business (Core) · Suggested Time: 15-20 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 17

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Review and summarize the eight steps in the accounting cycle (i.e., analyze originating transaction data, journalize, post, prepare worksheets, prepare financial statements, journalize and post adjusting and closing entries, prepare post-closing trial balance) for a merchandising business.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Distinguish differences in the accounting cycle for a merchandising business versus a service business.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify what source documents include (e.g., till tape, invoices, memos, cash receipts, cheque stubs) in a merchandising business.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Justify that no entry should be made unless it has a supporting document as related to the GAAP objectivity principle.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Analyze each source document and journalize appropriately for a merchandising business.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Execute a multi-journal system and/or an expanded combination journal (e.g., sales, purchases, cash receipts, cash payment) for a scenario/simulation of a merchandising business.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Post values to the general ledger and subsidiary ledgers such as accounts receivable and accounts payable.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Total and prove journal(s) debit columns equal credit columns.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Examine ways to prove the accuracy of posting (e.g., schedule of accounts payable, schedule of accounts receivable).

outcomes.statement: Implement steps 4-8 of the accounting cycle for a merchandising business.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 19: Steps 4-8 of Accounting Cycle for Merchandising Business (Core) · Suggested Time: 15-18 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 18

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Prove the accuracy of the general ledger for a merchandising business by preparing a trial balance.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Complete a worksheet by organizing and planning adjustments and sorting account balances into the correct financial statement columns to calculate the net income/loss.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Prepare a balance sheet, income statement and statement of owners' equity for a merchandising business.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Examine and discuss who reads financial statements and why they do.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Prepare the journal entries for adjusting and closing entries for the end of the accounting period in the general or synoptic/combination journal.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Post the adjusting and closing entries by transferring them from the journals to the general ledger to close the temporary accounts and prepare the business books for the next accounting period.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Prepare a post-closing trial balance to check the equality of the general ledger upon completion of the accounting cycle in a merchandising business.

outcomes.statement: Investigate payroll for a business.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 25B: Advanced Payroll (Optional) · Suggested Time: 6-10 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 25A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Itemize payroll components including earnings, compulsory and voluntary deductions.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Justify why detailed payroll records must be maintained.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify the data (e.g., hourly wage, salary, piecework, commission, overtime, contract work) typically used to calculate earnings for gross pay.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Prepare a payroll chart using provided financial information.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Calculate gross pay, total deductions and net pay based on the earnings for the correct pay period.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Differentiate between mandatory and voluntary optional deductions for employees.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Recognize that the compulsory deductions are an employer's expense to the federal government.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Calculate compulsory deductions (i.e., Canada Pension Plan, Employment Insurance, Federal Income Tax) and voluntary deductions using the taxable earnings based on government set percentages.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Discuss employers’ responsibilities regarding dispersing voluntary deductions to appropriate organizations (e.g., charitable donations).

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Explain the employers’ legal obligations for submitting income tax collected from employees.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Journalize and post the payroll to update general ledger accounts.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Discuss the importance of accurate payroll information for the preparation of year-end summaries (e.g., T4 and T4-A slips).

indicators.label: m
indicators.text: Analyze the importance of an employer completing a Record of Employment, with appropriate codes, for employees in situations where employment ends, or the employee leaves due to pregnancy, injury, illness, adoption leave, layoff, or dismissal.

indicators.label: n
indicators.text: Generate a payroll for a business simulation, with or without accounting software.

outcomes.statement: Explore business taxes and taxation.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 26: Business Taxes and Taxation (Optional) · Suggested Time: 2-3 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 25B

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explain the employers’ legal obligations for submitting income tax collected from employees.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Categorize taxes (e.g., property tax, business tax) paid in order to run a business.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss the significance of provincial sales tax collection from consumers’ purchases to be remitted (paid) to the provincial government.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Examine the importance of GST (Goods and Services Tax) being collected and remitted to the federal government.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Prepare journal entries incorporating various types of taxes.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Analyze the purpose of municipal, provincial and federal taxes.

outcomes.statement: Investigate banking functions for business.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 27A: Business Banking (Optional) · Suggested Time: 4-6 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify banking services designed for business.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify commonly used terms such as service charges and interest rates within the financial services industry.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Analyze banking services and software designed to meet specific business needs (e.g., small business, online business).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Examine banking fraud and its impact on businesses.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Analyze the impact electronic banking has on business.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Differentiate between a chartered bank, a credit union, a trust company and other financial services in the community.

outcomes.statement: Analyze the importance of cash control in a business.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 27B: Banking for Business Controls (Optional) · Suggested Time: 2-3 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 5

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Recognize the purpose of the bank reconciliation as a method of cash control.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Prepare a bank reconciliation and update accounting records (journals, cheque stubs) after the reconciliation.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Compare a business reconciliation to a personal situation.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify the need for a set of internal cash control procedures for a business to protect against theft, waste and to ensure accurate data.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Examine and express one's own beliefs, values, and attitudes when handling ethical and unethical situations relating to cash and business practices.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Discuss how the frequency of cash transactions requires a cash receipts journal, cash payments journal, or a synoptic/combination journal to be used as the book(s) of original entry.

outcomes.statement: Investigate the purpose of having a petty cash fund.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 28: Petty Cash (Optional) · Suggested Time: 4-6 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Define petty cash fund and recognize the advantages of having such an account.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Justify practices for establishing and replenishing a petty cash fund.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Carry out a transaction in which petty cash is used as payment.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Discuss how a petty cash system can be adapted to different organizations and businesses.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Summarize and explain good cash control procedures within personal, community, and business situations.

outcomes.statement: Investigate technology as a tool to aid in the accounting process.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 29B: Technology Applications for a Merchandising Business (Optional) · Suggested Time: 7-10 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 18

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explain the various types and purposes of accounting software.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explore the use of computers and accounting software in merchandising business accounting.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify key issues to consider when dealing with software copyright and site licensing.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Examine the importance of restricting access to data by using a password/security system.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Propose solutions to accounting problems where accounting software has been used.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Review the accounting cycle of a merchandising business relating manual activities to those that may be performed using accounting software.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Investigate how merchandising businesses in the community use accounting software.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Carry out an accounting cycle for a merchandising business using accounting software.

outcomes.statement: Analyze how financial statements are used when making business decisions related to bad debt.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 31A: Asset Analysis (Optional) · Suggested Time: 2-4 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 19

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Generate a list of who (e.g., insurance agencies, Canada Revenue Agency, financial institutions) needs access to financial statements and discuss the purpose of granting access.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Define bad debts and depreciation as used within financial statements.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss how bad debts, depreciation, and inventory valuations assist in assuring that assets are represented as accurately as possible on financial statements.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explore the inquiry questions: Who is interested in the accurate calculations of assets? Is it practical to aim for no bad debts in every situation? What impact does Canada Revenue Agency have on the amount of bad debt a company may claim?

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Assess the impact of the GAAPs (e.g., historical cost, adequate disclosure, matching revenue with expenses, consistent reporting) on what is reported on financial statements.

outcomes.statement: Examine bad debts expense using the allowance method.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 31B: Bad Debts (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 31A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Define write-off using the allowance method and direct write-off.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Differentiate between a write-off and a direct write-off.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explain the purpose of the allowance method for recording losses from uncollectible accounts.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Compute the amount of estimated bad debt for a business and prepare adjusting entries using the aging and percentage of net sales methods.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Perform the entries for writing off an uncollectible accounts receivable, using the write-off from an allowance account method.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Account for the collection of an account receivable that was written off.

outcomes.statement: Examine depreciation of fixed assets through journals and fixed asset records.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 31C: Depreciation (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 31B

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Describe the function of depreciation as connected to journal entries.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify accounting concepts, principles, and practices (e.g., historical cost, matching revenue expenses, obsolescence, salvage value, book value) related to fixed assets.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Define fixed assets and describe how the amount of depreciation is calculated.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Analyze how accounting for depreciation affects fixed assets.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Compute the amount of estimated depreciation expense and prepare journal entries using the straight-line method of depreciation for full and partial years.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explore and differentiate methods such as declining- balance, sum-of-the-years digits, production-unit method, and capital cost allowance for calculating depreciation.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Prepare journal entries for the disposal of fixed assets which have an accumulated depreciation account, calculating for each situation, disposing for a gain, a loss and at book value.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Calculate and record depreciation of fixed assets in a journal and fixed asset records.

outcomes.statement: Examine accounting practices through a project simulation related to a merchandising business.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 37: Merchandising Business Project (Optional) · Suggested Time: 7-10 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 19

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Organize and plan an accounting system that could be implemented given a set of a real life numerical examples such as phone bill, utility bills, business license, or rent.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Perform the financial responsibilities necessary to implement a chosen accounting system.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Examine the inquiry question: How do the accounts of a merchandising business differ from a service business?

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Review the accounting cycle for a merchandising business.

outcomes.statement: Prepare for the work placement.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 80A: Work Study Preparation (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explain the roles and responsibilities of each partner (e.g., student, parent, teacher or other school staff, employer) involved in the work placement.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Research the business/organization to become familiar with its operations.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: In collaboration with all partners, develop personal and learning goals for the work placement.

indicators.label: d
e
indicators.text: Compile an employer information package that includes documents needed for the work placement (e.g., personal career documentation such as a resume or portfolio, permission forms, logs, self- and employer evaluation forms).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text:
Brainstorm a list of questions to ask the employer before beginning the work placement; these may include:
- What is my schedule of work hours?
- Who is my supervisor?
- What should I wear?
- When will I be provided with safety training?
- What potential hazards might I encounter in the work placement?
- Where do I find fire extinguishers, first aid kits and emergency assistance?
- What type of safety gear am I expected to wear? Is it provided?
- What should I do if I get injured or have an accident in the workplace?
- How can I contact my health and safety committee or representative?
- Are there any health and safety procedures I should follow?
- Who is the first aid person?
- Where are safety notices posted?
- What should I do in case of a fire or emergency?

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Develop a list of questions that could potentially be asked by the employer/work placement in an interview situation as well as answers to the questions.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Participate in an interview with the employer prior to beginning the work placement.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Reflect upon one’s performance during the interview.

outcomes.statement: Participate in a work placement experience.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 81A: Work Study Placement (Optional) · Suggested Time: 25-50 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 80

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Apply relevant skills and abilities during the work placement experience.

indicators.label: b
c
indicators.text: Document knowledge and awareness of employment standards, safety, workplace ethics, rights and responsibilities, occupational health and safety, and networking observed during the work placement.

outcomes.statement: Relate one’s work placement experience to personal and career goals.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 82A: Work Study Follow-up (Optional) · Suggested Time: 2-4 hours · Level: Intermediate, Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 81A, B

indicators.label: a
b
indicators.text: Reflect on the attainment of personal and learning goals.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Update personal career documentation (e.g., resume, portfolio) following the work placement.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: In appreciation prepare a letter, note, card or other communication for the work placement employer.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Develop and/or revise personal and career goals based on the work placement experience.

outcomes.statement: Develop an awareness of the agriculture industry.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 1: Agriculture Industry Overview (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-5 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explore the history of the agriculture industry in Saskatchewan.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify the different sectors (e.g., crops, livestock, fisheries, apiculture and fruit farming) of the agriculture industry.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Investigate the percentage of residents of Saskatchewan who are employed in the agriculture industry.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify the types (e.g., seeding, application, harvesting and tillage) and specific examples (e.g., air seeder, sprayer and combine) of equipment used in agriculture.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Research and create a representation (e.g., timeline and infographic) of important dates in the history of the development of agricultural equipment (e.g., tractors and ploughs).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Conduct an inquiry to identify the variety of agricultural equipment designed for different industries (e.g., apiculture, dairy farming, poultry farming, vegetable and fruit farming).

outcomes.statement: Apply safety standards to prevent injuries in the agricultural equipment technician workspace.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 2A: Personal Safety (Core) · Suggested Time: 4-8 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss worker and employee rights and responsibilities as they relate to workplace safety and how they can prevent injuries.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify common safety hazard categories and hierarchy of control common to the agriculture equipment service industry.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Assess and mitigate the risks (e.g., slips, trips, falls, burns) and potential safety hazards (e.g., exposure to chemicals, gasoline, diesel) in the agricultural technician workspace.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Research the benefits of completing the different certifications and programs offered by Work Safe Sask, Sask Safety Council, Motor Safety Association, Agricultural Health and Safety Network, Sask Prevention and the Ministry of Labour Relations and Workplace Safety.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify and explore basic safety procedures (e.g., storage and maintenance of tools, clean workspace and caution when working at high heights and around large equipment) as they apply to an agricultural equipment technician.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Develop a list of rules for workplace safety including proper personal protective equipment (PPE), sanitation, neat and tidy work area and reporting workplace accidents and safety incidents.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Identify the dangers of working in a confined space (e.g., sprayer tank, combine grain tank and barn manure tank or pit).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Demonstrate the utilization and maintenance of protective devices on equipment.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Perform proper lockout and de-energizing of equipment before beginning inspections or repairs.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Identify the advantages and disadvantages of using each category of industry standard personal protective equipment (PPE) for respiratory, hearing, sight and body protection such as masks, ear plugs or earmuff, safety goggles and shields, gloves, footwear and aprons.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Demonstrate PPE cleaning procedures.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Describe hazards from the misuse of oxy-acetylene welding equipment (e.g., tanks, hoses and gauges) and take measures to avoid unintentional injuries caused by flashback and backfire.

indicators.label: m
indicators.text: Locate and demonstrate the correct use of safety equipment (e.g., eye wash station, shower, first aid station, shop ventilation, fire extinguishers and caging devices) in the workplace.

indicators.label: n
indicators.text: Post and maintain emergency phone numbers in a visible location.

indicators.label: o
indicators.text: Discuss appropriate actions in the event of an injury in the workplace, including whom to contact, how to report and first-aid procedures.

outcomes.statement: Investigate proper handling of hazardous materials to prevent injury in the workplace.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 2C: Hazardous Materials (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-5 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Describe the importance of and methods used to maintain a clean workplace.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify hazardous materials and relevant Workplace Hazardous Materials Information System (WHMIS) procedures to manage them in the workspace.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Investigate Occupational Health and Safety (OH&S) regulations for the storage of hazardous wastes.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe and utilize the four parts of WHMIS 2015 (i.e., hazard identification and product classification, labels with warning symbols, safety data sheets (SDS), worker education and worksite specific training) to handle hazardous materials safely.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Investigate the correct environmental handling, cleanup and waste disposal of lubricants (e.g., oil and grease), coolants, fuel, filters, cleaners, containers and tires in accordance with local bylaws and provincial guidelines.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Identify control measures according to the hierarchy of controls, to prevent exposure to hazardous wastes and toxic chemicals.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Examine the methods used to remove and dispose of chemical residue (e.g., fertilizer and pesticide spray) from application equipment.

outcomes.statement: Examine proper handling of equipment to ensure biosecurity and food safety.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 2E: Biosecurity and Food Safety (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-5 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Examine the importance of ensuring biosecurity in agricultural industries.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Outline the management practices that should be put in place when working with agricultural equipment to ensure biosecurity.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe the correct environmental handling, cleanup and disposal of waste products found in agricultural equipment being serviced.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Recognize how the Safe Foods for Canadians regulations and Canada Good Agricultural Practices (GAP) program may affect a repair technician’s process in servicing agricultural equipment.

outcomes.statement: Explore the characteristics of large equipment in the agriculture industry.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 3A: Large Equipment (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-10 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 1

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify hazards and safety practices outlined in an operator’s manual for individual large equipment.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Investigate the historical development of different traction devices (e.g., tires, tire configurations and tracks) found on agricultural equipment.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify and explain the operation of the major components (e.g., steering, suspension, brakes, drive train, cooling, lubrication and mechanical parts of implements) of agricultural equipment.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explore the purpose of different tractor attachments (e.g., front-end loader and 3-point-attachment) and their effect on tractor stability, control and center of gravity.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Investigate the development of specific implements (e.g., bale shredder, baler and combine) to simplify tasks in the agriculture industry.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explore the development of agricultural equipment (e.g., harrow, air seeder, planter and manure spreader) designed to improve the output of crop land.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Describe the operation of the different headers (e.g., pickup, flex-draper and auger) used on a combine.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Identify the characteristics of different power transmission systems (e.g., power take off, hydraulic and electric) and the hazards associated with their operation.

outcomes.statement: Investigate the function of small equipment used in agricultural operations.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 3B: Small Equipment (Optional) · Suggested Time: 2-5 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify hazards and safety practices outlined in an operator’s manual for individual small equipment.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify the dangers of working in a confined space with agricultural equipment.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explore the identity and operation of different small equipment (e.g., windmills, water pumps and electric generators) used in agricultural operations.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify the purpose of smaller tractors in the agricultural industry.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Explain the function and hazards of different attachments for utility tractors.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Describe the purpose of different transportation equipment (e.g., side-byside and all-terrain vehicle [ATV]) and regulatory requirements of their use in the agriculture industry.

outcomes.statement: Apply safe work practices when using and maintaining hand and power tools.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 4: Hand and Power Tools (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-10 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Demonstrate safe work practices when working with hand and power tools including the use of PPE recommended by the tool manufacturer and equipment including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Assess and mitigate risks related to the use of hand and power tools.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Investigate correct storage for hand and power tools according to the manufacturer.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Classify tools according to their capabilities (e.g., cutting, shock, holding and torsion) and method of power (e.g., hand, power and electric).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify power tools according to power delivery (e.g., pneumatic, battery and AC) measured in torque.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Demonstrate the selection and use of the correct tool for a specific task.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Demonstrate the correct use of multimeters and circuit testers, including scale on the equipment, when working with electric circuits.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Identify the function of the components and safety procedures in using an oxy-acetylene torch.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Describe and perform the accepted start-up and shut-down procedures for an oxy-acetylene system including required PPE.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Describe how heat transmits through attached systems to prevent fire and damage to other components.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Understand and describe how to heat metal bolts and pulleys to remove them and cut mild steel including the correct flame, flame distance, angle of the tip, direction of travel, speed of travel, and motion of tip.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Inspect tools for damage and tag for repair as instructed by the supervisor.

outcomes.statement: Identify, select and use fasteners properly.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 5: Fasteners (Core) · Suggested Time: 1-2 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Follow safe work practices when using fasteners, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Classify agricultural equipment fasteners into common categories (e.g., bolts, nuts, clips, pins, rivets, screws and washers).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify fasteners based on specifications such as metric/SAE, grade, length, diameter and thread pitch or count.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe types (e.g., 12-point, carriage bolt, hex and Torx) of fastener heads commonly found in agricultural applications.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Explore how adhesives and sealants are used as fasteners for agricultural equipment and how some of them are not compatible if mixed.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Select and use appropriate tools to manipulate fasteners.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explain the importance of torque values and tightening sequence of specific fasteners.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Adjust and utilize torque wrenches to properly tighten fasteners.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Utilize a tap and die set to complete thread repair of damaged fasteners.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Select and use appropriate tools to extract broken fasteners.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Describe the use and effect of commercially available products to assist with the removal (e.g., penetrating oil) or securing of fasteners (e.g., Loctite).

outcomes.statement: Investigate the characteristics of agricultural equipment lubricants.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 6: Lubricants (Core) · Suggested Time: 1-2 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss the functions and properties of lubricants.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Distinguish between synthetic and non-synthetic lubricants.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Demonstrate how to add a lubricant to specific fittings.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe the purpose of different oil service ratings (e.g., API service ratings, SAE viscosity grades and original equipment manufacturer [OEM] specifications).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Describe the function of various oil additives (e.g., limited slip and oil stabilizers).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Summarize the ways in which oil can be contaminated and the potential effects on an engine.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Demonstrate the safe, environmental handling and disposal of lubricants and containers.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Identify occupational hygiene practices (e.g., using petroleum resistant gloves and barrier creams) when handling petroleum products to prevent absorption into skin.

outcomes.statement: Explore the structure, function and operation of an agricultural equipment dealership.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 7A: Agricultural Equipment Dealerships (Core) · Suggested Time: 4-8 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 3A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify the brands of agricultural equipment sold in Saskatchewan and the specific dealerships that operate in the local area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Tour an equipment dealership in person or virtually.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Examine the layout of the dealership including the buildings for the organization of employees and service of equipment and the property to maximize space for the storage and sale of equipment.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Investigate the variety of services offered by the dealership.

indicators.label: e
f
indicators.text: Examine the fixed costs of materials (e.g., overalls, tools, wipes and power) for the technicians at a dealership.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Discuss how the technician’s quality of workmanship (e.g., communication with customers and commitment to the job) affects the dealership.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explain how leased equipment changes how a dealership operates their business.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Explore the importance of efficiency in a technician’s work habits to reduce producer down time and increase productivity of a farming operation.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Investigate the importance of confidentiality, ethics, digital citizenship and communication skills when working in an agricultural equipment dealership.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Discuss the current and future trends in the functions, structure and operation of agriculture equipment dealerships.

outcomes.statement: Demonstrate safe procedures to lift and support agricultural equipment.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 8: Agricultural Equipment Lifting and Support (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-10 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Perform safe personal and mechanical lifting utilizing industry practices related to agricultural equipment, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Maintain an inspection record for jacks, stands, straps and chains.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify balance and lift points for different types of agricultural equipment.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Recognize the capabilities, limitations and applications of mechanical lifting devices (e.g., floor and transmission jack, lift, hoist, pulley system, strap, chain, and mobile, truck and overhead cranes) and safety devices available on the job site.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify required lifting and support devices needed for a specific task.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Determine the safest position to place agricultural equipment before lifting.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Lift and lower agricultural equipment in a safe manner using the appropriate lifting devices.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Discuss the limitations of the human body in lifting materials or equipment and the ergonomic best practices to avoid injury.

outcomes.statement: Investigate basic agricultural equipment maintenance procedures.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 9A: Introductory Agricultural Equipment Maintenance (Core) · Suggested Time: 4-8 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explore the safety procedures identified by the manufacturer related to agricultural equipment maintenance.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe common procedures for periodic inspection and testing of agricultural equipment.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Select lubricants and filters for different agricultural equipment and service conditions according to manufacturers’ specifications.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Locate and follow manufacturer’s lubrication and maintenance schedules.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss the benefits of using a regular maintenance schedule for agricultural equipment.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Describe the service intervals, specifications and maintenance requirements to maintain a manufacturer’s warranty.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Recognize, inspect and adjust basic components (e.g., tires, bearings, belts, fuel, air filters, fluid levels and lights) of agricultural equipment that require periodic inspection and/or lubrication.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Identify, replace or repair and confirm the repair of minor broken parts.

outcomes.statement: Perform appropriate advanced agricultural equipment maintenance procedures safely and correctly.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 9B: Advanced Agricultural Equipment Maintenance (Core) · Suggested Time: 10-20 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 9A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Follow the manufacturer’s safety guidelines when performing advanced agricultural equipment maintenance procedures, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe and demonstrate processes used to identify faults in the components of agricultural equipment.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Conduct a visual inspection of agricultural equipment including tire pressure and condition, lights, fluid levels, condition of hoses, belts, pulleys and battery.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Carry out drivetrain (e.g., differential, engine, transmission and transfer case) lubricant and filter changes following manufacturer’s specifications.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Demonstrate manufacturer recommended system maintenance such as checking spark plugs, positive crankcase ventilation valves and valve adjustments.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Inspect and replace faulty bearings and seals while following safe work processes.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Inspect, repair and confirm the repair of a driveline with worn and faulty parts while following safe work processes.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Investigate the types of interactive diagnostic tests of agricultural equipment such as dynamometer test, engine cylinder cut-out test and emission system fault codes.

outcomes.statement: Explore the processes involved in the diagnosis, service and repair of agricultural equipment tracks, tires and wheels.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 10: Tracks, Tires and Wheels (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-10 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify safe work practices (e.g., lifting heavy parts, proper inflation process and recognition of cut and pinch points) when working with agricultural equipment tracks, tires and wheels, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain how track and tire condition affects the handling, fuel economy and safety characteristics of agricultural equipment.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Compare the advantages and disadvantages of using tracks or tires on agricultural equipment.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe the design, construction and purpose of different tracks, tires and wheels including tire sidewall information.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify common physical and mechanical issues in the operation of agricultural equipment tracks.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Evaluate track and tire condition (e.g., tread depth, rubber condition and wear patterns) and explain causes and effects of rubber damage, wear and defects.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explain the purpose of and when track and tire service (e.g., tire rotation and balancing and track replacement) is required.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explain the parameters (e.g., caster, camber and toe) that affect wheel alignment and how misalignment can affect agricultural equipment handling and tire wear.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Inspect tracks for wear and proper adjustment as per the manufacturer’s specifications and discuss how improper adjustment can cause safety concerns.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Inspect lug nuts for proper torque as per the manufacturer’s specifications and discuss how improper torque and mounting can cause safety concerns.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Describe the design, construction and hazards associated with tires mounted on a split rim (locking ring).

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Follow correct environmental procedures for recycling and disposal of tires.

outcomes.statement: Investigate diagnostic service processes for agricultural equipment storage batteries.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 11: Storage Batteries (Optional) · Suggested Time: 2-5 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Follow the manufacturer’s safe work practices when working with storage batteries, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify the manufacturer’s requirements for the voltage, size, shape and quantity of batteries required for specific agricultural equipment.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe the construction and operation of common types (e.g., absorbent glass mat [AGM] and lead acid) of agricultural equipment storage batteries.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify cold cranking amperes (CCA) and reserve capacity minutes of storage batteries.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Perform service tests (e.g., check voltage and load) on storage batteries.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Follow safe procedures including connection order when performing battery replacement, boosting and charging operations.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Describe and diagnose common battery failures (e.g., frozen, sulfated and short circuits).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Follow correct environmental procedures for recycling and disposal of storage batteries.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Identify emergency procedures for first aid and cleanup of ruptured batteries.

outcomes.statement: Explore the function and operation of electrical circuits.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 14A: Fundamentals of Agricultural Equipment Electrical Systems (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-10 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Follow safe work practices (e.g., avoid sharp material and hot parts or tools) when working with electrical circuits, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe major electrical concepts including basic atomic structure and conductor, insulator and semi-conductor materials.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Define current, resistance and voltage and state their units of measurement.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Discuss the factors (e.g., wiring, connection quality and corrosion) that affect resistance and their effect on current and voltage.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Differentiate between AC and DC circuits and identify where they are used in electrical circuits in agricultural equipment.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Distinguish between the characteristics of series, parallel and series-parallel electrical circuits.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Identify different types of switches and their purpose.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explain the purpose of a controller area network binary unit system (CANBUS).

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Classify common types of electric motors.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Diagnose, repair and confirm the repair of electrical circuits by soldering, splicing and taping wires and connections.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Assess the quality of and adjust electrical repairs.

outcomes.statement: Investigate the operation, diagnosis and repair of small engines.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 16: Small Engines (Optional) · Suggested Time: 10-15 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices in dangerous situations (e.g., shock hazards, hot and sharp surfaces and moving parts) when working with small engines, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain the working principles of an internal combustion engine.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Differentiate between the operation of 2-stroke and 4-stroke engines.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explain the construction and function of the 5 C’s (i.e., camshaft, connecting rod, crankshaft, cylinder block and cylinder head) of major engine subassemblies

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Describe how improper cooling and lubrication can cause engine failure.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Identify specialized measuring equipment used to measure specific engine parts (e.g., pistons, cylinders and cam shaft).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Define and determine engine measurements (e.g., clearance, out of round and taper) that are used to assess an engine.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explain how repair manuals are used to disassemble, repair and reassemble engines.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Demonstrate how to disassemble and reassemble an operational small engine.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Verify correct assembly by following manufacturer’s procedures to start, run and stop a small engine.

outcomes.statement: Explore the construction and operation of multicylinder engines.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 17: Industrial Engine Theory (Optional) · Suggested Time: 10-15 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 16

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Investigate common agricultural engine configurations (e.g., inline and Vtype).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Define and determine agricultural engine measurements (e.g., displacement, compression ratio and clearance).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Differentiate between common valve train configurations (e.g., in block and single or dual overhead camshaft) in agricultural engines.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe the components and function of major, multi-cylinder engine subassemblies (e.g., cooling, exhaust, fuel and lubrication systems).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Explain the variations (e.g., cam lift, piston shape and ring design) of internal engine components.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Compare the air flow of naturally aspirated and forced air turbocharged diesel engines.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Compare how fuel is supplied and ignited in spark ignition gasoline engines and compression ignition diesel engines.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Describe the advantages and disadvantages of different fuel sources used in agricultural engines.

outcomes.statement: Examine engine charging systems.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 18: Charging Systems (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-10 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 14A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices (e.g., disconnect battery, prevent grounding of live wires, and be aware of sharp surfaces and cleaning agents) when working with agricultural equipment charging systems, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Find and identify components (e.g., alternator, batteries and voltage regulator) of an engine charging system.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe the function and operation of an engine charging system and its components.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Use appropriate equipment like a multimeter or battery load tester to test engine charging systems.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Diagnose, repair and confirm the repair of common charging systems faults (e.g., alternator failure, damaged or loose belts and poor connections) following manufacturer recommendations.

outcomes.statement: Investigate engine starting systems.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 19: Starting Systems (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-10 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 14A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Follow safe work practices (e.g., disconnect battery, prevent grounding of live wires, and be aware of sharp surfaces and cleaning agents) when working with engine starting systems, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify and find the components (e.g., battery, ignition switch, starter motor, solenoid, starter relay and safety lockout switch) of an engine starting system.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss the function and operation of an engine starting system.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe the operation of a starter including the starter activation and drive mechanisms.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify common faults and symptoms associated with engine starting system malfunctions.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Perform tests on engine starting systems using appropriate equipment like multimeters.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Discuss how to use voltage drop to test a starter.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Diagnose, repair and confirm the repair of common starting system faults (e.g., control circuit failure, starter failure and poor connections).

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Perform safety checks to ensure equipment does not move unintentionally when performing starter system tests.

outcomes.statement: Explore the components and operation of agricultural equipment power trains.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 22: Power Train (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify the components of agricultural equipment power trains.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explore the types of transmissions (e.g., mechanical, semi-powershift, powershift, hydrostatic and continuously variable) used in agricultural equipment.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Differentiate between torque and horsepower.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explain the theory behind the power output (e.g., speed versus torque) of transmissions.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Describe the purpose and operation of the power take-off on agricultural equipment.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explain how final drives and differentials operate.

outcomes.statement: Investigate agricultural equipment steering systems.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 23: Steering Systems (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices in dangerous situations (e.g., dangers of welding or heating steering linkage components) when working with agricultural equipment steering systems, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Compare the operation and components of linkage and hydrostatic steering systems.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explain the parameters camber, caster and toe that affect wheel alignment.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe how misalignment can affect agricultural equipment handling and tire wear.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Describe how wear or damage to steering components can affect handling, steering control and wheel alignment.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Inspect and assess steering components for corrosion, damage, excessive play and wear.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Discuss how improper torquing can be a safety issue when replacing steering components.

outcomes.statement: Investigate agricultural equipment brake systems.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 25: Brake Systems (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-10 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 24

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices in dangerous situations (e.g., contact with asbestos dust from brake components and contact of brake fluid with eyes and painted surfaces) when working with agricultural equipment brake systems, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b

outcomes.statement: Prepare for the work placement.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 80A: Work Study Preparation (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Intermediate, Advanced · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text:
Describe and reflect on the three basic rights that all workers have under Part III – Occupational Health and Safety in The Saskatchewan Employment Act, 2019:
- the right to know - the hazards at work and how to control them;
- the right to participate - in finding and controlling workplace hazards; and,
- the right to refuse – work that you believe is unusually dangerous

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain the roles and responsibilities of each partner (e.g., student, parent, teacher or other school staff, employer) involved in the work placement

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Research the business/organization to become familiar with its operations.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: In collaboration with all partners, develop personal and learning goals for the work placement.

indicators.label: e
f
indicators.text: Compile an employer information package that includes documents needed for the work placement (e.g., personal career documentation such as a resume or portfolio, permission forms, logs, self- and employer evaluation forms).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text:
Brainstorm a list of questions to ask the employer before beginning the work placement; these may include:
- What is my schedule of work hours?
- Who is my supervisor?
- What should I wear?
- When will I be provided with safety training?
- What potential hazards might I encounter in the work placement?
- Where do I find fire extinguishers, first aid kits and emergency assistance?
- What type of safety gear am I expected to wear? Is it provided?
- What should I do if I get injured or have an accident in the workplace?
- How can I contact my health and safety committee or representative?
- Are there any health and safety procedures I should follow?
- Who is the first aid person?
- Where are safety notices posted?
- What should I do in case of a fire or emergency?

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Develop a list of questions that could potentially be asked by the employer/work placement in an interview situation as well as answers to the questions.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Participate in an interview with the employer prior to beginning the work placement.

indicators.label: j

outcomes.statement: Apply proper handling of hazardous materials to prevent injury in the workplace.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Demonstrate the importance of, and methods used for, maintenance of a clean and safe workplace.

indicators.text: Identify important information categories from product labels, Material Safety Data Sheets (MSDS) and manufacturer's chemical information packages such as compatibility, storage requirements, application method, preharvest intervals and withdrawal periods.
