outcomes.statement: Examine strategies for managing transitions in life.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 1: Transitions in Life (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify examples of transitions (e.g., starting or ending a relationship, graduation from high school, having or adopting a child, starting a new job) experienced throughout life.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Discuss potential positive and negative impacts transitions can have on self and others such as family, friends and community.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Reflect on personal position in the life cycle (i.e., birth to death) and describe the transitions (e.g., first day of school, moving from elementary to high school, death of a loved one, moving to a new community, first job) already experienced.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Create a personal representation (e.g., timeline, roadmap) that illustrates transitions experienced and reflect on the impact each has had on self and others.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Predict some of the transitions (e.g., moving, moving in with roommates, starting post-secondary education, getting a first or new job) a person may encounter in the near future.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Interview family, community members, Elders or Knowledge Keepers to discuss the transitions experienced in life and the influences (e.g., role models, family, culture) and strategies (e.g., seeking the advice of others, being prepared) that have helped cope with each transition.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Develop a list of strategies (e.g., accepting change, being prepared, focusing on the positives) for dealing with transitions in life.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Discuss skills required to manage various life changes.

outcomes.statement: Examine how self-awareness informs career planning and goal setting.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 2: Self-Awareness (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-4 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Create an inventory of personal values, interests, personality traits, skills, abilities, learning styles, strengths and weaknesses.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Research the purpose of a variety of personal inventories or selfassessment tools such as Myers-Briggs and True Colours.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Complete a variety of personal inventories and reflect on the results.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify various career pathways that align with one’s interests, skills and abilities.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Explore how self-awareness can inform career planning and goal setting.

outcomes.statement: Explore effective decision-making processes.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 3: Decision-Making (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 2

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explore factors (e.g., personality, risk, culture) that influence decision-making.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Evaluate the effectiveness of various decision-making styles (i.e., agonizing, compliant, delaying, fatalistic, impulsive, intuitive, paralysis, planning) with respect to their effectiveness.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify criteria (e.g., identification of alternatives, risk assessment, predicted results) useful in evaluating the effectiveness of decisions.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Construct a decision-making model or process that could apply to a variety of different types of decisions.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Develop a list of personal characteristics that influence decision-making.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Analyze important decisions (e.g., moving, attending post-secondary, entering the workforce, relationships) that will be made in the immediate and distant future.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Reflect on past decisions and use criteria to determine whether the best choices were made.

outcomes.statement: Explore how goal-setting supports achievement.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 4: Goal Setting (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-4 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 3

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss the importance of setting goals and of personal accountability for achieving those goals.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explore reasons (e.g., unexpected events, health emergency, loss of employment, changing priorities) for adjusting goals.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Debate the value of adjusting rather than abandoning a goal.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Research the characteristics of various goal-setting models.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Create a personally relevant SMART (i.e., specific, measurable, attainable, relevant and time-based) goal and monitor progress.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Develop an action plan to achieve a SMART goal.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Analyze tools such as vision boards, bucket lists, journaling and action plans that can assist with setting goals, achieving goals and/or accountability.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Identify short and long-term goals (e.g., personal, career, family/relationship, financial) for achieving a desired lifestyle.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Share goals and plan with a supportive person (e.g., Elder, family member, teacher, peer) to receive feedback.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Reflect on feedback received and adjust goals and plans accordingly.

outcomes.statement: Investigate the importance of personal safety to health and well-being.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 5: Personal Safety (Core) · Suggested Time: 4-5 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify potential risks to personal health and security as a result of overreliance on personal devices (e.g., hearing loss due to overuse of audio devices, injury to self and others due to distracted driving).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Discuss ways to ensure personal safety and the safety of others in a variety of social situations (e.g., attending a social event with a friend rather than alone, applying media awareness when participating in social media conversations, displaying awareness of danger to self and others).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify areas (e.g., public transportation, hospitality industry) that are potentially associated with exploitation, sexual exploitation and human trafficking of children and youth.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Investigate the risk factors (e.g., race, age, gender, marginalised groups, socio-economic status) related to grooming for exploitation, sexual exploitation and human trafficking of children and youth.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Analyze potential risks associated with sharing personal information on social media, including those related to privacy and security.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Describe precautions (e.g., logging out of and closing online sessions, keeping private information about banking, passwords or absences from home) used to protect personal information online.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explain how to access and communicate with support people (e.g., counselors, medical professionals, police) in an emergency situation.

outcomes.statement: Investigate the importance of physical safety to health and well-being.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 6: Physical Safety (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-4 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify potential risks to physical safety as a result of emergencies and natural disasters (e.g., wildfire or grassfire nearing community, house fire due to unsafe cooking habits, imminent tornado or flooding).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Discuss ways to ensure fire safety in a variety of home and social situations (e.g., safe barbecuing and cooking tips, appropriate fire extinguishing, electrical safety).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe emergency preparedness for a variety of scenarios such as severe weather, power outages and fires.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explain how to access emergency and fire safety information and communications (e.g., highway hotline, weather channel, SaskAlert, emergency phone numbers, muster points) during an event.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Research the possible effects or consequences (e.g., injury, loss of property, death) of being unprepared for a variety of possible emergencies.

outcomes.statement: Investigate ways to care for and maintain items that support living independently.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 7: Care and Maintenance of Personal Items (Optional) · Suggested Time: 7-10 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Locate and identify laundry care symbols found on clothing and other fabric items such as towels, sheets and blankets.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain the four laundry care categories (i.e., washing, drying, dry-cleaning, ironing).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss ways (e.g., repairing, maintaining, donating) to extend the use of items such as clothing, household appliances and vehicles.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Demonstrate safe and proper use of household equipment and appliances (e.g., washing machines, dryers, irons, dishwashers, stoves and ovens).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Develop a plan, incorporating safe and effective strategies and products, for regular cleaning of commonly used areas in the home (e.g., kitchen, bathroom, living room, bedroom).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explore options for sharing responsibilities (e.g., doing dishes, cleaning the bathroom, snow removal, garbage removal) with roommates to enhance safety and enjoyment of shared living accommodations.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Propose strategies for keeping living areas free of pests (e.g., bed bugs, ants, rodents) and propose possible solutions to resolve pest issues independently and with the support of landlords and service providers.

outcomes.statement: Identify food choices that impact personal and community well-being.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 10: Food Choices (Core) · Suggested Time: 7-10 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Examine personal and external factors (e.g., availability, religion, affordability) that influence food choices.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Investigate the impact of diets and personal food choices on personal well-being.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Investigate available community resources (e.g., food banks, community kitchens, school meal programs, community gardens) that provide additional access to nutritious and affordable foods.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explore costs of various meals (e.g., self-prepared, meal subscription boxes, restaurants).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Estimate the cost of eating a healthy, balanced diet (e.g., fresh fruit and vegetables, lean protein, whole foods).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Research the variance in food costs based on international, national, provincial, territorial and regional geography.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Examine the possible health consequences (e.g., cardio-vascular disease, hypertension, diabetes) of long-term consumption of food with low nutritional value.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Compare nutrition fact tables (e.g., carbohydrate, fat, protein) of similar food items and their possible impact on personal well-being.

outcomes.statement: Assess personal understanding and self-awareness of equity, diversity and inclusion.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 12: Equity, Diversity and Inclusion (Core) · Suggested Time: 7-10 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explore what constitutes diversity (e.g., race, ethnicity, culture, gender, ability).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Investigate an aspect of social inequity in the community (e.g., income, housing, health care, systemic barriers).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Analyze the purpose of Canada’s Employment Equity Act with a focus on the passage “no person shall be denied employment opportunities or benefits for reasons unrelated to ability”.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Determine how individuals are influenced by norms, trends, images and values about equity, diversity and inclusion in a variety of scenarios.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Analyze how sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender, gender expression and perceived gender influence opportunities and interactions.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Recognize what privilege is and how it relates to gender, race and social class.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Identify inclusive language and behaviours related to diversity and equity in a variety of settings.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Recognize, name and challenge instances of inequity, bias, intolerance and discrimination.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Explore how to become an ally to support positive and inclusive change.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Assess how community diversity enhances the well-being of self, family and community.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Examine personal and collective actions to make institutions, workplaces and communities more welcoming and inclusive to diverse populations.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Investigate the effects of intersectionality on the experiences of people.

outcomes.statement: Explore self-care resources, services and products available in Saskatchewan.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 13: Health Self-Care (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify self-care resources, services and products available in the community.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Examine situations (e.g., headache, missed menstrual cycle, depression) when care is required including life-threatening situations and long-lasting or unusual symptoms.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explore resources (e.g., emergency room visit, extended hours medical clinic, pharmacist consultation, family doctor, HealthLine 811) to access medical attention and the processes to obtain these services.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe possible self-care actions (e.g., exercise program, nutrition plans, sleep plans) and benefits and challenges of these actions.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Describe possible self-care products and the benefits and challenges of these products.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Investigate the eligibility requirements, claims processes and services (e.g vision, dental, prescription) available through the provincial government health insurance plan, federal programs (i.e., Non-Insured Health Benefits Program and Interim Federal Health Program) and private or employerfunded health insurance plans.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Identify skills required to self-advocate when accessing health-care products and services (e.g., developing health care directives, indicating organ donation wishes, researching alternatives, gaining second opinions).

outcomes.statement: Analyze elements of strong and healthy relationships.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 16: Relationships Basics (Core) · Suggested Time: 7-10 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss various types of relationships (e.g., family, friend, professional).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify key elements (e.g., honesty, trust, support, independence) that form the basis of healthy relationships.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Investigate various cultural norms and customs (e.g., multi-generational households, Indigenous kinship systems) in relationships.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Examine the ways in which relationships can positively or negatively affect personal physical and emotional well-being.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Explore how positive or negative peer pressure (e.g., bullying, gangs, teamwork) can have an impact on self-esteem.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Analyze how the use of technology (e.g., social media, gaming, texting) can affect interpersonal relationships.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Investigate causes of conflicts (e.g., role expectations, personality clashes, spiritual/cultural beliefs) within relationships.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Discuss how effective communication is important in maintaining, strengthening and ending relationships.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Explore the importance of clear, honest communication regarding sexual contact in a dating relationship.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Define sexual consent and how it can be communicated.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Explore possible implications (e.g., legal, physical, emotional) of sexual behaviour without consent.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Recognize characteristics (e.g., jealousy, resentment, dishonesty, control) of toxic relationships.

indicators.label: m
indicators.text: Develop strategies to end toxic relationships.

indicators.label: n
indicators.text: Examine behaviours associated with sexual harassment (e.g., cat-calling, making sexual comments about a person’s body, using unwanted pet names).

indicators.label: o
indicators.text: Investigate factors (e.g., finances, children, living arrangements, emotions) that impact decisions to end a relationship.

indicators.label: p
indicators.text: Explore community supports (e.g., counselling, mediation) available for people seeking help with relationships.

indicators.label: q
indicators.text: Explore ways to move forward after the end of a relationship.

outcomes.statement: Analyze factors that influence life balance.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 18: Understanding Life Balance (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Inquire into what it means to have personal, family, community and work life balance.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explore influences (e.g., career, recreational activities) on life balance.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Examine a variety of cultural approaches to achieving life balance.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explore healthy behaviour patterns (e.g., exercise, sleep, good hygiene, proper nutrition) in balancing personal, family, community and work life in order to reduce effects such as burn out, depression and stress.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Examine the importance of quality sleep and the effects (e.g., irritability, fatigue, energy) of lack of sleep.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Discuss potential challenges of excessive time spent on digital devices and impacts on intellectual, physical, emotional and spiritual well-being.

indicators.label: g

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Assess personal time management practices and identify common time wasters.

outcomes.statement: Investigate holistic approaches to mental wellness.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 23: Mental Wellness (Core) · Suggested Time: 12-15 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Examine the meaning of holistic well-being and how mental health fits into that definition.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Assess personal current levels of wellness through inventories that address multiple dimensions (e.g., mental, spiritual, emotional and physical) of wellness.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Examine the interactions and interconnectedness between the dimensions of wellness (e.g., mental, spiritual, emotional and physical) and how they impact mental health.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Analyze various predisposing or precipitating factors (e.g., loss of a loved one, finances, chemical imbalance, life transitions and trauma) that contribute to mental illness.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text:
Examine signs and symptoms of stress such as:
- emotional (e.g., burnout, irritability, anxiety);
- mental (e.g., constant worry, difficulty concentrating); and,
- physical (e.g., headache, muscle aches, sleep disturbance).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Research potential mental health challenges tied to disorders (e.g., Autism Spectrum Disorder, Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorder, Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder) and the services and supports available in the local community and in Saskatchewan.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Investigate supports in the local community to maintain positive mental wellness.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Examine the effects that traumatic experiences (e.g., residential schools, religious and cultural persecution, serious accidents or illnesses) can have on individuals and communities.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Identify risky behaviours (e.g., drug use, gang affiliation, toxic relationships, alcohol, self-harm) that can be symptomatic of mental illness.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Analyze how Western, Indigenous, traditional, complementary and alternative approaches to health care can contribute to a holistic perspective of mental wellness.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Investigate the positive mental health effects that can be achieved through developing a connection with nature.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Discuss consequences (e.g., embarrassment, shame, resentment) of stigmas and misconceptions of mental health within society.

indicators.label: m
indicators.text: Contrast the episodic nature of mental illness with fluctuation in moods.

indicators.label: n
indicators.text: Discuss valuable skills (e.g., positive self-perception, stress management, positive social network, resilience) for maintaining mental wellness.

indicators.label: o

outcomes.statement: Investigate the effects of addiction on the health and well-being of individuals and community.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 25: Addictions (Core) · Suggested Time: 7-10 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss various types of substance and behavioural addictions (e.g., gambling, drugs and alcohol, vaping, social media).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Analyze the effects of addiction on everyday life (e.g., physical health, mental health, personal finances).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify the potential impacts of the overuse of social media (e.g., mental wellness, anxiety, depression, negative effect, cyber bullying, quality of sleep) on self, individual and community well-being.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Inquire into biological factors (e.g., genetics, mental illness, age) that can contribute to risk of addiction.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Explore reasons why (e.g., relaxation, trauma, curiosity) an individual might choose to consume addictive substances.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Identify signs and symptoms of addiction.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Examine the characteristics of resilience and how it can help prevent or mitigate addiction.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Examine how social pressure (e.g., culture and norms, popularity) can influence addictive behaviours.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Identify intergenerational patterns of addiction and examine how these patterns can contribute to ongoing addiction.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Inquire into addiction from spiritual, personal, cultural and community points of view.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Investigate how distorted thinking and behaviour contribute to addiction.

b
c

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify resources available to consumers to assert their rights.

indicators.label: e

indicators.label: f

outcomes.statement: Explore the rights and responsibilities associated with Canadian citizenship.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explore individual rights and responsibilities related to citizenship in Canada’s Charter of Rights and Freedoms.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Analyze responsibilities related to citizenship (e.g., obeying the law, paying taxes, serving on a jury, knowing local treaty territory and history, recognizing the spirit and intent of treaties, participating in local community) as a treaty person and Canadian citizen.

indicators.text: Examine one’s position regarding the importance of the treaty relationship for the social, cultural and economic prosperity of all Saskatchewan and Canadian people.

outcomes.statement: Apply principles and techniques for injury prevention to ensure safety in the work area.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 1B: General Safety (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-5 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Recognize and apply safe and fair work practices including freedom from violence, harassment and bullying.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Reflect on personal and collective responsibility for, and commitment to, promoting and supporting workplace safety.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify industry standard personal protective equipment (PPE) such as safety goggles, footwear, hearing and respiratory protection, headwear and protective clothing.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Review the fire evacuation plan for the work practices including the location of fire alarms, fire extinguishers and exits.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Describe ways to reduce personal injury or material and equipment damage resulting from unsafe work practices or environments.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Discuss appropriate actions in case of an injury or accident, such as whom to contact and first-aid procedures.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explain the purpose of ventilation in a confined environment as it relates to controlling air quality (e.g., welding fumes, plastic off-gas and cutting, fluid misting).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Identify hazardous materials and relevant Workplace Hazardous Materials Information System (WHMIS) procedures.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Describe the importance of a clean work area and methods used to maintain a clean work area.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Identify risks and potential safety hazards (e.g., tools on floor, exposed live wires and extension cords).

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Describe the hierarchy of controls to control hazards and mitigate risks in machining workspaces and environments.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Describe control measures using the hierarchy of controls to limit risks of expected physical hazards associated with machining (e.g., workstation ergonomics, slip, trips and falls, repetitive strain).

indicators.label: m
indicators.text: Demonstrate an understanding of procedures (e.g., safety inspections and audits that include ergonomics of workspace lay-outs) to ensure safe practices in the machining workspace.

outcomes.statement: Apply safe work practices in the machine shop.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 2B: Machining Safety (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 1B

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify potential safety hazards (e.g., electricity, chemicals, rotating machines, ventilation and noise) in the machining work environment.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Demonstrate consistent and effective use of personal protective equipment (PPE) to ensure personal safety and the safety of others in the workspace.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss processes involved in good housekeeping procedures and routines in the machine shop.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Locate fire extinguishers, the eye-wash station and the first-aid station in the work environment.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify preventative measures to avoid specific accidents common to machining equipment and environments.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Recognize potential hazards presented by tools and equipment in the machine shop.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Demonstrate safe usage of all tools and equipment.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Create an emergency evacuation plan to safely leave the machine shop.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Discuss the process involved in reporting near-misses or accidents.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Demonstrate safe practices when working with jigs and fixtures.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explore industrial efficiencies created by using jigs and fixtures.

indicators.label: f

indicators.label: g

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Observe safe and efficient operation of a lathe.

indicators.text: Demonstrate effective use of required personal protective equipment (PPE) when using a lathe.

indicators.text: Identify safety features of a lathe.

indicators.text: Critique the efficiency of ground tools on different materials.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text:
Describe and reflect on the three basic rights that all workers have under Part III - Occupational Health and Safety in The Saskatchewan Employment Act,2019:
- the right to know - the hazards at work and how to control them;
- the right to participate - in finding and controlling workplace hazards; and,
- the right to refuse - work that you believe is unusually dangerous.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain the roles and responsibilities of each partner (e.g., student, parent, teacher or other school staff, employer) involved in the work placement.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Research the business/organization to become familiar with its operations.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: In collaboration with all partners, develop personal and learning goals for the work placement.

indicators.label: e
f
indicators.text: Compile an employer information package that includes documents needed for the work placement (e.g., personal career documentation such as a resume or portfolio, permission forms, logs, self- and employer evaluation forms).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text:
Brainstorm a list of questions to ask the employer before beginning the work placement; these may include:
- What is my schedule of work hours?
- Who is my supervisor?
- What should I wear?
- When will I be provided with safety training?
- What potential hazards might I encounter in the work placement?
- Where do I find fire extinguishers, first aid kits and emergency assistance?
- What type of safety gear am I expected to wear? Is it provided?
- What should I do if I get injured or have an accident in the workplace?
- How can I contact my health and safety committee or representative?
- Are there any health and safety procedures I should follow?
- Who is the first aid person?
- Where are safety notices posted?
- What should I do in case of a fire or emergency?

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Develop a list of questions that could potentially be asked by the employer/work placement in an interview situation as well as answers to the questions.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Participate in an interview with the employer prior to beginning the work placement.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Reflect upon one’s performance during the interview.

outcomes.statement: Participate in a work placement experience.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 81A: Work Study Placement (Optional) · Suggested Time: 25-50 hours · Level: Intermediate, Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 80A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Apply relevant skills and abilities during the work placement experience.

indicators.label: b
c
indicators.text: Document knowledge and awareness of employment standards, safety, workplace ethics, rights and responsibilities, occupational health and safety, and networking observed during the work placement.

outcomes.statement: Relate one’s work placement experience to personal and career goals.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 82A: Work Study Follow-up (Optional) · Suggested Time: 2-4 hours · Level: Intermediate, Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 81A

indicators.label: a
b
indicators.text: Reflect on the attainment of personal and learning goals.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Update personal career documentation (e.g., resume, portfolio) following the work placement.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Prepare a letter, note, card or other communication for the work placement employer, expressing appreciation.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Develop and/or revise personal and career goals based on the work placement experience.

outcomes.statement: Analyze the relationship between marketing and business or organizational success.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 1: Introduction to Marketing (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Define marketing.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe the areas that marketing entails beyond selling and advertising.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss who (e.g., businesses, government, school teams or clubs and notfor-profits) might engage in marketing and their reasons for doing so.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Differentiate between commercial (i.e., for a fictitious or real-life brand) or social (i.e., for behaviour change around a social issue) marketing.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify examples of commercial (e.g., Saskatchewan Roughriders) and social (e.g., ending mental health stigma or promoting the use of seatbelts) marketing.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explain the concepts of brand and branding and the relationship between branding and marketing.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explore the relationship between satisfying consumers and meeting organizational goals (e.g., profit or changed behaviour).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Discuss strategies (e.g., communicating, exceeding expectations, asking for feedback and showing appreciation) for building good customer relationships and creating value for consumers.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Relate marketing to competing effectively, much like a sports team plays to its strengths.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Summarize reasons (e.g., importance to business or organizational success, career opportunities and being an informed consumer) for studying marketing.

outcomes.statement: Examine factors that impact a business or organization’s marketing activities.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 2: The Marketing Environment (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 1

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Describe what is meant by the marketing environment.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Examine forces (i.e., demographic, socio-cultural, economic, technological, competitive and regulatory) that influence the marketing environment.

indicators.label: c
d
indicators.text: Research the purpose of, and ways to conduct, an environmental scan.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Assess the current state of demographic, socio-cultural, economic, technological and regulatory forces locally, provincially, nationally and globally for a variety of products.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Predict the future impact of demographic, socio-cultural, economic, technological and regulatory forces on marketing activities for the same products.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Discuss the importance of understanding and constantly monitoring the marketing environment for successful and effective marketing.

outcomes.statement: Analyze the relationship between consumer behaviour and marketing.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 3: Consumer Behaviour (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 1

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss the importance of understanding consumer behaviour for effective and successful marketing.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Discover how and why consumer behaviour can change over time.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Examine the relationship among Maslow’s Hierarchy of Needs, consumer behaviour and marketing.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe the five stages (i.e., problem recognition, information search, evaluation of alternatives, purchase decision and post-purchase behaviour) of the purchase decision process that a consumer goes through in making purchasing decisions.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Reflect on personal experiences with the purchase decision process.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text:
Examine factors that influence consumer buying behaviour including:
- situational (e.g., reason for making a purchase; social surroundings such as others present at the time of purchase; physical surroundings such as background music, decor and crowding; the time of day or amount of time the consumer has available; timing of the purchase [e.g., last-minute]; and the consumer’s mood);
- psychological (e.g., motivation, personality, perception, lifestyle, attitudes and beliefs); and,
- socio-cultural (e.g., word of mouth and opinion leaders; reference groups such as family, friends, celebrities or athletes; culture and subcultures).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Identify examples of referral marketing (e.g., Uber share codes or refer a friend promotions).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explain the concept of buyer’s remorse and its potential impact on both buyers and the sellers.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Research ways (e.g., a coupon towards a future purchase, loyalty cards/programs and money-back guarantee) marketers attempt to reduce buyer’s remorse.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Explain the components of the AIDA model including Attention, Interest, Desire and Action.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Relate the AIDA model to marketing strategies that capitalize on consumer behaviour.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Reflect on ways that consumer behaviour can affect individuals as well as others in all aspects of life (e.g., at home, at work, at play and at school).

outcomes.statement: Analyze strategies for successfully creating, marketing and managing a brand.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 4: Successful Brands (Core) · Suggested Time: 7-10 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 1

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Describe the concept of a brand.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Differentiate between brand identity and brand image.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss the importance of a strong brand image and a brand identity that resonates with consumers.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Examine the characteristics of a purpose-driven brand, including its potential impact on consumer behaviour.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Explain personal reasons for identifying with, and finding inspiration from, specific brands.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explore the concept of brand positioning.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Identify types of brand positioning strategies such as cost-driven positioning, niche product positioning or quality of service positioning.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Assess the brand positioning strategies used by a variety of successful brands such as the Saskatchewan Roughriders.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Describe the concept of brand extension.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Provide real-life examples of brand extensions (e.g., a tech brand such as Apple adding watches to its product line).

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Examine the concept of brand personality and the emotional response it intends to elicit in consumers.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Reflect on personal experiences with, and responses to, brand personalities.

indicators.label: m
indicators.text: Describe the concept of brand voice.

indicators.label: n
indicators.text: Identify real-life examples of brand voice used in the marketing of a variety of products.

indicators.label: o
indicators.text: Describe the concept of brand relationship.

indicators.label: p
indicators.text: Examine strategies for building strong brand relationships with customers including community building.

indicators.label: q
indicators.text: Discuss the importance of a brand recognizing, and differentiating itself from, competitors.

indicators.label: r
indicators.text: Justify the importance of effective online reputation management (ORM).

indicators.label: s
indicators.text: Propose strategies (e.g., answering promptly to online feedback/comments, encouraging satisfied customers to submit online reviews and owning up to mistakes) for effective and successful ORM.

indicators.label: t
indicators.text: Research instances when a brand’s reputation was damaged including the reasons for the reputational damage, the brand’s response and the resulting outcome.

outcomes.statement: Examine personal branding.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 5: Personal Branding (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 4

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Describe personal branding.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explore the components (e.g., who one is, what one stands for, the values one embraces and the ways in which one expresses those values) of a personal brand.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify elements (e.g., authenticity and consistency) of a successful personal brand.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Discuss how a personal brand can be impacted by online behaviour, including social media use.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Reflect on one’s personal brand including brand identity, image and voice.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Create a self-representation that depicts one’s personal brand and share it with a trusted friend, adult or family member.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Examine the relationship between personal and professional branding.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Recommend ways to establish and build a positive personal brand.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Describe the personal brand of at least one individual considered to be personally inspirational.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Research instances when personal brands have been negatively impacted and the reasons for each situation.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Develop a plan for maintaining or building one’s personal brand.

outcomes.statement: Investigate components of the traditional marketing mix.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 6A: The Traditional Marketing Mix (Core) · Suggested Time: 10-15 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 2

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify the elements of the traditional marketing mix, also known as the 4 Ps (i.e., product, price, place and promotion).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain the application of the traditional marketing mix to a social marketing campaign.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Differentiate between products that are tangible (e.g., goods) and intangible (e.g., services, ideas or experiences).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Categorize local businesses or organizations according to the types of products they offer.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss reasons (e.g., meeting a basic need or contributing to a desired lifestyle) why customers purchase a particular product.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Assess the importance of offering a product that meets or exceeds customer expectations.

indicators.label: g
h
indicators.text: Assess the effects of pricing a product too high or pricing it too low.

indicators.label: i
j
indicators.text: Discuss the importance of offering a product in the right place and at the right time.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text:
Research considerations for product placement, such as:
- where potential customers are located;
- where and how potential customers shop (e.g., retail location and online); and,
- where the competition places their products.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Examine the role of promotion in gaining the attention of consumers and motivating them to take action (e.g., purchase a product or change behaviour).

indicators.label: m
indicators.text: Identify paid (e.g., radio or television advertisements, print media and social advertisements) and free (e.g., organic social media and word of mouth) promotional opportunities.

indicators.label: n
indicators.text: Compare features of push and pull marketing.

indicators.label: o
indicators.text: Identify real-life examples of push and pull marketing.

indicators.label: p
q
indicators.text: Investigate advantages (e.g., global reach, cost efficiency and measurable results) and disadvantages (e.g., security and privacy issues, timeconsuming, and skills and training required) of online promotion.

indicators.label: r
indicators.text: Examine the application of the 4 Ps for a business, organization or brand/product of personal interest.

outcomes.statement: Investigate components of the extended marketing mix.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 6B: The Extended Marketing Mix (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 6A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify the three additional Ps (i.e., people, process and physical evidence) that have been added to the traditional marketing mix to create the extended marketing mix.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain the reasons (e.g., easier to apply to services and the advent of online marketing and e-commerce) for the creation of the extended marketing mix.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe various roles (e.g., salesperson, marketing team and customer service representative) that are considered part of the people element of the extended marketing mix.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Discuss desirable characteristics (e.g., effective and perceived positively by customers) associated with people roles in the extended marketing mix.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Examine the role of brand voice in the people “P” of the extended marketing mix.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Reflect on personal or observed positive and negative people experiences as a customer.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explore the process element of the extended marketing mix.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Research desirable characteristics (e.g., efficiency, reliability and sustainability) of effective processes in the extended marketing mix.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Identify examples (e.g., packaging, websites, and branding such as logos on employee uniforms and awards) associated with the physical evidence element of the extended marketing mix.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Examine the application of the extended marketing mix for a major global brand.

outcomes.statement: Analyze the use of digital and traditional marketing strategies.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 7: Digital and Traditional Promotion (Core) · Suggested Time: 7-10 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 2

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Differentiate between traditional (e.g., print, television, direct mail and outdoor advertising such as signage) and digital marketing (i.e., online).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify visible applications of traditional and digital marketing within the community.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Relate traditional and digital marketing to the promotion “P” in the marketing mix.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Assess advantages and disadvantages associated with traditional and digital marketing.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Examine the relationship between user behaviour (i.e., of the target audience) to the selection and application of traditional and/or digital marketing strategies.

indicators.label: f
g
indicators.text: Assess the impact on marketing strategies of limitations (e.g., blocking of cookies) imposed by digital platforms.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Examine the use and impact of animation and video in modern marketing.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Defend the use of traditional, digital, or a hybrid of both types of marketing for a variety of given marketing scenarios.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Identify ways that consumer behaviour (e.g., online or through SMS) can be tracked and leveraged for marketing purposes.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Examine the types of consumer information that can be tracked through digital marketing.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Debate the ethics of tracking and leveraging consumer behaviour for marketing purposes.

indicators.label: m
indicators.text: Describe the concept of advertising avoidance.

indicators.label: n
indicators.text: Discuss actions (e.g., not sharing information, blocking pop-up advertisements on the computer and unsubscribing from newsletters) that consumers can take to avoid viewing or receiving advertising.

indicators.label: o
indicators.text: Propose ways in which marketers can effectively deal with consumer advertising avoidance.

indicators.label: p
indicators.text: Investigate the origins, evolution and impact of influencer marketing to the present day.

indicators.label: q
indicators.text: Conduct an inquiry into the process for becoming, and succeeding as, an influencer marketer.

indicators.label: r
indicators.text: Propose marketing strategies that may be effective to reach consumers of the future.

indicators.label: s
indicators.text: Develop a plan for promoting a business, brand or product of personal choice as an influencer marketer.

outcomes.statement: Assess the importance of market research for successful and effective marketing.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 8: Market Research (Core) · Suggested Time: 7-10 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 3

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss the purpose and importance of ongoing market research for effective and successful marketing.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain the correlation between market research and the ability to make sound business or operational decisions.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Examine the importance of identifying and monitoring the competition as part of initial and ongoing market research.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Define qualitative and quantitative research.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Describe ways in which qualitative and quantitative research might be conducted and how the results might be used in marketing research.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Differentiate between primary and secondary market research.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Identify ways (e.g., observations and surveys such as pop-up or omnibus) in which primary data can be gathered.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Discuss the advantages (e.g., less costly than primary research and easier/quicker to gather) and disadvantages (e.g., datedness and reason for collecting may not align with one’s purposes) of secondary research.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text:
Identify sources of secondary data such as:
- government departments, libraries, business incubators and chambers of commerce (public and generally free);
- trade associations and research firms (commercial and generally associated with subscription or association fees); and,
- colleges, universities, technical institutes (academic).

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Describe ways to confirm the credibility of sources of secondary data as well as the accuracy of that data.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Explain the concept of a target market.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Describe what market segmentation is and why it is beneficial.

indicators.label: m
n
indicators.text: Investigate how marketers use buyer personas to drive marketing success.

indicators.label: o
indicators.text: Outline the steps for creating a buyer persona.

indicators.label: p
indicators.text: Develop several buyer personas, including one for self.

indicators.label: q
indicators.text: Describe marketing strategies that would be effective with potential customers, including self, for a variety of products.

outcomes.statement: Assess the importance of ethical and socially responsible behaviour and marketing.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 9: Ethics and Social Responsibility (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 3

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Define ethics.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text:
Describe good ethics in business as it relates to relationships between, but not limited to:
- businesses and customers;
- businesses and suppliers; and,
- employers and employees.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Assess the importance of regulations for both consumers and businesses.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Research the evolution and resulting impact of privacy and consumer protection laws on marketing practices in Saskatchewan and Canada.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Describe the importance of ethical behaviour and business ethics as they relate to ethical marketing.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Identify examples of types of false or misleading advertising such as bait and switch, price deception, unsubstantiated claims and misleading photos or illustrations.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Summarize the standards for marketing in Canada as detailed by the Canadian Marketing Association Code of Ethics and Standards.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Discuss the relationship among purpose-driven marketing, ethics and social responsibility.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Examine social responsibility and the benefits (e.g., to the business, consumer, society, the environment and others) of having a socially responsible marketing strategy.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Analyze the impact of marketing strategies used by local, provincial (e.g., tentree), national (e.g., Manitobah Mukluks) and international (e.g., The Body Shop, Toms, and Proctor and Gamble—Dawn Soap) companies that promote themselves as being socially responsible.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Research ways (e.g., Certified B Corporations) to verify a company’s claim of being socially responsible.

outcomes.statement: Examine the importance of inclusive marketing.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 10: Inclusive Marketing (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Modules 4, 9

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Describe inclusive marketing.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain accessible marketing as a component of inclusive marketing.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Research ways that marketing content can be more easily accessed by users of all abilities (e.g., audio or larger text for individuals with vision impairments, print for individuals with hearing impairments and digital content for individuals with motor impairments) or by users with limited access (e.g., print materials or television content for individuals with no or limited access to the Internet).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Discuss the impact that inclusive marketing can have on a brand (e.g., creating loyalty and trust) and on others (e.g., giving voice to a marginalized group).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss the importance of cultural understanding in developing effective and culturally sensitive marketing content.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Differentiate between cultural appropriation and cultural appreciation.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Examine the potential impact of using cultural appropriation and cultural appreciation in marketing campaigns.

indicators.label: h
i
indicators.text: Explain, and provide examples of, stereotype marketing.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Justify stereotype marketing as an exclusive, rather than inclusive, marketing strategy.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Brainstorm examples (e.g., a dad making dinner or a mom fixing a lawn mower) of marketing that challenge stereotypes.

outcomes.statement: Examine the relationship between marketing and customer experiences.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 11: Customer Experience Marketing (Optional) · Suggested Time: 2-3 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 2

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Differentiate between customer service and customer experiences.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain what customer-centric marketing means and the importance of a business or organization knowing and understanding its customers.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Examine the benefits (e.g., greater brand loyalty and improved customer retention) of such marketing efforts.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Discuss the importance of monitoring, managing and responding to online and other reviews.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Propose strategies for replying to both positive and negative online reviews.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Identify the stages (e.g., pre-purchase, purchase and post-purchase) of a customer journey map.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explore effective marketing strategies for connecting with consumers at each of the stages.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Reflect on personal encounters with poor and exemplary customer experiences.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Describe characteristics of ideal customer experiences.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Assess the role that marketers play in creating and supporting the ideal customer experience through customer experience marketing.

outcomes.statement: Investigate careers in marketing.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 12: Careers in Marketing (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Modules 1, 6A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Research opportunities and trends in marketing careers in Saskatchewan, Canada and the world.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Compare the marketing services offered by a variety of Saskatchewan-based marketing or advertising companies.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Examine the roles, responsibilities, educational qualifications and personal and professional qualities typically required by those who work in marketing.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text:
Generate a list of questions to ask a professional in the marketing industry to learn about their work; questions may include:
- What do you do?
- What knowledge and skills do you use every day?
- What does a typical day look like for you?
- What is the most interesting marketing project you have worked on?

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: List personal interests, skills, abilities and traits that may lead to a career in marketing.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Research which marketing occupations are facing shortages and which are oversubscribed locally, regionally and/or provincially.

indicators.label: g
h

outcomes.statement: Examine the benefits of a positive health and safety culture in the marketing workplace.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 13: Health and Safety in the Marketing Workplace (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 12

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss the impact of a workplace injury on the injured and others including the employer, work colleagues, family and friends.

indicators.label: b
c
indicators.text: Describe the importance and benefits of a positive health and safety culture at work.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Define a workplace hazard.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify potential physical hazards (e.g., exposure to allergens such as perfumes and other scents, sitting for long periods of time and eye strain) associated with office work.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Research causes of stress and anxiety (e.g., little or no results from a marketing campaign and time pressures) for those working in marketing careers.

indicators.label: g
h
i
indicators.text: Compare the hazards associated with working remotely to working in an office environment.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Explain why some brands align themselves with safety messaging such as Mission Zero.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Develop a marketing campaign that promotes a positive health and safety culture in the marketing workplace.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Reflect on personal and collective responsibility for, and commitment to, developing and supporting a positive health and safety culture at work.

outcomes.statement: Examine characteristics and components of a strategic marketing plan.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 14A: Strategic Marketing Plan A (Core) · Suggested Time: 10-15 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Modules 6A or 6B, 7, 8, 9

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explain a value proposition.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify examples of value propositions presented by several brands.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Examine the relationship between a value proposition and strategic marketing.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Discuss the importance and interrelatedness of the marketing mix (i.e., traditional or extended) for strategic marketing.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Research tenets of an effective marketing campaign such as consistency (e.g., of message, brand, tone and relevancy), frequency (e.g., of message; less effective advertisements require more frequency) and creativity (e.g., amusing; engaging; and featuring well-designed imagery, video or text).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Describe the purpose of a marketing plan.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Assess characteristics (e.g., organized, easy to read, clear section headings and free of grammar or spelling errors) of prepared strategic marketing plans.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Analyze the impact of finances on a marketing plan.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text:
Describe the elements of prepared marketing plans, such as:
- market analysis (e.g., purpose and mission of the business or organization; description of current markets and strategies; primary competitors; and SWOT [i.e., strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats] analysis);
- marketing strategy (e.g., goals and expected outcomes, target market description, marketing mix); and,
- implementation (e.g., activity schedule including responsibilities, schedule and budget; evaluation procedures including evidence of success and methods of collecting the evidence).

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Identify reasons for changing or recalibrating a marketing plan.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Develop a commercial or social marketing plan with a budgetary limit.

outcomes.statement: Develop, implement, manage and evaluate the success of a marketing campaign.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 14B: Strategic Marketing Plan B (Optional) · Suggested Time: 15-20 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 14A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Research companies and organizations (e.g., local businesses, not-forprofits and school or community clubs and teams) as potential clients or beneficiaries for a marketing campaign.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Assess the pros and cons of the various companies and organizations researched to determine the best option(s) for a project.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Analyze marketing strategies used by companies and organizations that are considered competitors.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Collaborate with the chosen company or organization to develop a marketing plan.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Implement the marketing plan.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Monitor the implementation of the marketing plan and make adjustments, as required, throughout the process.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Conclude and evaluate the success of the marketing campaign based upon the criteria outlined in the marketing plan.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Reflect on personal contributions to, and personal growth resulting from, developing, implementing, managing and evaluating the marketing campaign.

outcomes.statement: Prepare for the work placement.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 80: Work Study Preparation (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 6A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text:
Describe and reflect on the three basic rights that all workers have under Part III – Occupational Health and Safety in The Saskatchewan Employment Act, 2019:
- the right to know – the hazards at work and how to control them;
- the right to participate – in finding and controlling workplace hazards; and,
- the right to refuse – work that you believe is unusually dangerous.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain the roles and responsibilities of each partner (e.g., student, parent, teacher or other school staff, employer) involved in the work placement.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Research the business/organization to become familiar with its operations.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: In collaboration with all partners, develop personal and learning goals for the work placement.

indicators.label: e
f
indicators.text: Compile an employer information package that includes documents needed for the work placement (e.g., personal career documentation such as a resume or portfolio, permission forms, logs, self- and employer evaluation forms).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text:
Brainstorm a list of questions to ask the employer before beginning the work placement; these may include:
- What is my schedule of work hours?
- Who is my supervisor?
- What should I wear?
- When will I be provided with safety training?
- What potential hazards might I encounter in the work placement?
- Where do I find fire extinguishers, first aid kits and emergency assistance?
- What type of safety gear am I expected to wear? Is it provided?
- What should I do if I get injured or have an accident in the workplace?
- How can I contact my health and safety committee or representative?
- Are there any health and safety procedures I should follow?
- Who is the first aid person?
- Where are safety notices posted?
- What should I do in case of a fire or emergency?

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Develop a list of questions that could potentially be asked by the employer/work placement in an interview situation as well as answers to the questions.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Participate in an interview with the employer prior to beginning the work placement.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Reflect upon one’s performance during the interview.

outcomes.statement: Participate in a work placement experience.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 81: Work Study Placement (Optional) · Suggested Time: 25-50 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 80

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Apply relevant skills and abilities during the work placement experience.

indicators.label: b
c

outcomes.statement: Relate one’s work placement experience to personal and career goals.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 82: Work Study Follow-up (Optional) · Suggested Time: 2-4 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 81

indicators.label: a
b

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Update personal career documentation (e.g., resume, portfolio) following the work placement.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Prepare a letter, note, card or other communication for the work placement employer, expressing appreciation.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Develop and/or revise personal and career goals based on the work placement experience.

outcomes.statement: Perform common automotive diagnosis and repair processes.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 2: Automotive Diagnosis and Repair Processes (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-3 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices when performing automotive diagnosis and repair, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe common practices and procedures involved in automotive repair.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify steps (e.g., identify, diagnose, repair and confirm the repair) common to automotive diagnostic processes.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Use appropriate service information to identify proper repair processes for a specific problem.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify required components, and compile a parts list and cost estimate, for a specific repair or modification process.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Discuss the benefits of preventive maintenance of an automobile.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Conduct a visual inspection of an automobile, including tire pressure and condition, lights, fluid levels, condition of hoses, belts and battery.

outcomes.statement: Apply principles and techniques for injury prevention to ensure safety in the automotive workplace.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 3B: Automotive Safety Equipment, Hazardous Materials, and Housekeeping Skills (Core) · Suggested Time: 4-12 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify the importance of safety when undertaking automotive service procedures, including safety hazards and preventative measures common to the automotive industry.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe ways to reduce personal injury or material and equipment damage as a result of unsafe work acts or environments.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Inspect and utilize protective devices on equipment.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify industry standard personal protective equipment (PPE), such as safety goggles, hearing protection, gloves and footwear, and appropriate PPE cleaning procedures.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify potential health concerns when PPE is not used properly.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Identify the correct fire extinguisher for different classifications (i.e., A, B, C, D and K) of fires and how to use the extinguisher correctly (i.e., PASS - Pull Aim Squeeze Sweep).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Describe the importance of a clean workplace and methods used to maintain a clean workplace.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Locate, identify and explain the correct use of safety equipment (e.g., eye wash station and first aid station) in the workplace.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Identify, label, store and handle hazardous materials according to Workplace Hazardous Materials Information System (WHMIS 2015).

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Recognize and apply safe and fair work practices, including freedom from violence, harassment and bullying.
