outcomes.statement: Conduct an in-depth inquiry investigating a consistent theme or idea within a body of work demonstrating insight into ways that artists create in order to learn.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Set inquiry goals and parameters with teacher guidance that foster strengths and allow the investigation to shift or extend.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Initiate research by using art strategies, such as thumbnail sketches, annotated or illustrated text and maquettes, to explore, reveal and develop the inquiry.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Establish and apply safe studio practices that respect the health and well-being of everyone sharing the space.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Pursue varied responses to the inquiry, including storytelling through art, to demonstrate artistic competencies with concept, composition, execution and analysis.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Extend the investigation through independent study that explores related and/or unexpected questions inspired by other disciplines.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Reflect regularly on own portfolio and continue personal practice to develop artistic competencies, including pushing the boundaries of selected media.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Critique work for a focused, emotive message, skillful use of select media and varied visual arrangements relating to a strong underlying visual idea.

outcomes.statement: Invent and adapt style variations in new works influenced by selected artists.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Investigate a wide range of artworks, including those from other disciplines, for the maker’s influences and present findings about artistic integrity for class discussion.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Discuss artworks, along with possible controversy, that make use of appropriated imagery in the service of the artist’s intent.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Examine emerging trends, alternative media and current technologies in art and reflect on how information from the past and present may be integrated in own exploration of recurring themes.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Evaluate and apply methods to establish authenticity and avoid imitation such as making use of own photographs as source material, rendering imagery directly from life and using symbols or visual words to convey personal meaning.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss legal and ethical issues associated with art making and marketing (e.g., authorship, copyright, ownership, censorship, appropriation, use of responsible practices, respecting cultural/religious symbols or iconography).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Research plagiarism policies of universities, colleges, art schools and art programs.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Consult Indigenous Knowledge Keepers and artists to understand and develop respect for sacred imagery and practices of gifting learning.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Play with styles and approaches, while building skills and investigating own ideas.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Evaluate own portfolio for possible copyright infringement or the unethical use of the work of others, including using another medium to copy work, and refine or alter works as needed.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Explain how portfolio pieces show own ideas and evidence of significant development in work inspired by the creative property of other artists maintaining reference citations or visual bibliography.

outcomes.statement: Regularly document and develop own creative process (e.g., inspiration, research, sketches, production, media skills, evaluation, refinement) up to and including completed works.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Describe stages of own creative process and compare them to those used by practicing artists from a variety of fields.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Compile and photograph own creative products including methods for initiating new work through practice and research.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe and record own distinctive way of approaching a creative task to develop understanding of strengths and weaknesses of that approach.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Maintain a sketchbook or art journal containing initial sketches and drafts, research and reference work demonstrating persistence in skill development.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text:
Explore and experiment with additional methods to foster a broader creative process, including for example:
- flexibility with new media and technologies
- fluency in observational work including life drawing
- on-site art making during experiential field trips
- responses to visual culture and personal environment.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Compose own library of inspirational references, notations, artifacts, own photographs, media exploration, visual notes and other source materials inspired by surroundings, other artists and other disciplines.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Research and co-create criteria for the selection, storage and display of portfolio items (e.g., documentation in digital and other formats of one’s creative process and products, depth and breadth of ideas, media and techniques represented).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text:
Track own progress (e.g., new ideas, skills) and regularly record the development of work up to completion through well-composed photographs, including for example:
- selecting and photographing completed works for submission to external agency or post-secondary institution meeting their criteria for submission
- optimizing images for print, digital sharing, and/or display.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Evaluate effectiveness of creative process in developing works that demonstrate active risk-taking and thoughtful revision.

outcomes.statement: Produce works that purposefully and creatively manipulate compositional and design strategies to express a point of view or communicate an idea.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Research varied methods of visual organization and stylistic approaches and their cultural influences including those used by Indigenous artists.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Engage in a series of quick skill-building challenges to explore the effects of focusing on selected elements of art, principles of design and/or image development strategies.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Use one or more of these preliminary works as starting points for a more extensive piece.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Play with visual organization beyond implied boundaries of compositional rules (e.g., rule of thirds, rule of odds, rule of space, orientation, vantage point, geometry, focal point, rest areas) through directed studio practices.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Build a collection of work demonstrating increasing technical skill and consistent trial and error in manipulating the elements of art, principles of design and image development strategies.

outcomes.statement: Prepare and present own work in a professional manner to share ideas with wider audience.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Research the range of ways artists can promote and present their work for different audiences and different purposes.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Research exhibition opportunities for students initiated by local, global or online communities (e.g., performance piece, community project/show, website, social media, art competitions, etc.).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Co-construct and rank criteria for exhibition, including health and safety considerations, and apply to overall design within selected space.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Select works to exhibit that highlight own strengths.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Design exhibitions utilizing multimedia, lighting, sound, video and/or digital spaces.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Consider inclusive curatorial practices including purpose of show, selection process, exhibition space, matting work, producing advertising and show cards, when viewing a collection of art in a gallery or other exhibition space.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Articulate intentions of works and choices for overall show through exhibition text and curatorial rationale.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Document process and reflect on the impact of sharing work on self and the community.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Predict the future of visual art exhibitions considering factors such as diversity, inclusion and technological developments.

outcomes.statement: Examine and critically respond, orally and in writing, to the work of professional artists utilizing a range of art criticism models.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: View and evaluate professional art, including Indigenous art, by interacting with guest artists and by visiting galleries.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe initial reactions and responses and determine what the artist did to initiate that reaction in the viewer.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Compare and contrast selected artworks through analysis of formal concerns, societal perspectives and artist intentions.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Use a critical process to convey an informed opinion within a formal critique/research paper including properly cited sources.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Use the language of art and appropriate terminology when writing or discussing artworks.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Identify how design principles, image development strategies and elements and principles of design affect the overall impact of works selected for study.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Describe the visual language and conventions of the time period in which work was created.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Analyze connections between self and selected art works.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Inquire how different people respond to the same work in different ways and how that reflects life experiences, cultural context and world view.

outcomes.statement: Evaluate, for the purpose of improvement, own works in progress and completed works during regular critiques with peers.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Set norms for respectful understanding of diverse cultures and personal histories prior to beginning analytical discussion of student works.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Evaluate artwork against co-constructed criteria using art terminology.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe own decision making and problem-solving processes and reflect on the effectiveness of choices made.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Demonstrate an understanding of the complexity of communicating through art.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Use descriptive and constructive feedback making suggestions for improvements or extensions.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Determine which aspects of the work are most important to alter or revise and what makes an artwork most successful.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Suggest solutions to artistic problems and set goals during regular progress checks.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Articulate and assess own role in the creative process leading to the work under review.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Conduct a critical inquiry into own practice by reviewing creative process and portfolio development and share learning with peers.

outcomes.statement: Assess how knowledge is produced and shared in various ways through a range of art forms including those produced by First Nations and Métis artists.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Examine and interpret the work of First Nations and Métis artists to learn how knowledge is shared and culture is sustained across generations.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Differentiate between knowledge that is spiritual or sacred and knowledge that is secular and how these are represented in art (e.g., architecture, painting, craft).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe the significance of specific art works in shaping content or challenging assumptions in history, society or culture.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Research an artist whose work is personally meaningful and reflects aesthetic, cultural, historical or spiritual knowledge.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Describe how visual culture and personal history contribute to own practice and knowledge formation.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explore the interconnected relationship between the artist, the art and the viewer.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Make interdisciplinary links between art, science, technology, design and mathematics.

outcomes.statement: Research and discuss the business of art including supports offered by arts organizations.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Deepen understanding of gallery culture and community by visiting galleries and arts organizations and presenting career information to peers.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Research artist associations and supporters of the arts (e.g., Sask Arts, SaskCulture, Canadian Artists’ Representation/Le front des artistes canadiens, Organization of Saskatchewan Arts Council, Canada Council), artists’ guilds, artist-run centres and arts education organizations (e.g., Canadian Society for Education through Art, National Art Education Association).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Research the mandate of a gallery and investigate the roles of gallery personnel (e.g., curators, educators, conservators, director, communications office).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Co-construct health and safety procedures for using shared studio spaces.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Make community connections by meeting with local artists and/or business people to explore mentorship possibilities.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Document and present learning and outline plans for continuing connections as a practicing artist.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Reflect on experiences that will inform engagement and set the foundation for life-long learning in the arts.

evidence.observation: The outcomes page groups the outcomes under 6 unit headings.

outcomes.statement: Investigate the roles and responsibilities of theatre production team members.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 1A: Introduction to Theatre Production (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-6 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss the functions of theatre such as theatre that entertains, informs, documents, challenges and inspires.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text:
Generate and examine inquiry questions regarding the perceived value of theatre, such as:
- What makes theatre unique?
- Why do audiences continue to attend theatre after many hundreds of years?
- What do theatre production teams contribute to an audience’s experience?

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss the functions of theatre production teams (e.g., to bring artistic vision to life, to ensure production tasks are carried out in an aesthetically satisfying, safe, timely and cost-effective manner).

indicators.label: d
e
indicators.text: Identify and categorize team member responsibilities, discuss the collaborative nature of theatre production and co-develop school-based ‘company’ rules and procedures.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Create a visual representation (e.g., flowchart, map) to demonstrate relationships and interdependence among various theatre jobs.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Organize and maintain a learning log (i.e., theatre log) including items such as tasks, schedules, experiences and understandings, to support planning, self-reflection, documentation and evaluation of learning.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Identify and explore the responsibilities of production department heads.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Describe the relationships among department heads and theatre crews.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Investigate how theatres are funded (e.g., commercial, not-for-profit) and discuss the roles of producers and management teams in moving productions from inception to performance (e.g., licensing, budgeting, assembling creative and technical teams).

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Discuss similarities and differences between large and small theatre companies, considering the impact of the availability of resources (e.g., human and financial) on production.

outcomes.statement: Investigate how designers create and collaborate to bring a theatrical vision to life.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 1B: Collaborative Processes of Theatrical Design and Production (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-6 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 1A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Examine the collaborative nature of theatre.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Investigate ways that designers (e.g., set, costume, lighting, sound) get their ideas (e.g., identifying play requirements, researching, discussing with director).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Examine the roles of individuals and teams in production design.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Discuss functions of design areas (e.g., lighting to establish time, sound to reveal mood, set to establish place, costume to reveal character).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Investigate the purposes and content of various theatrical toolboxes or toolkits (e.g., lighting designer’s, costume designer’s).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explore and apply components of a designer’s toolbox (e.g., visual skills, use of maquettes, representation of mood, use of symbol/metaphor, light, colour, sound) for aesthetic purposes.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Analyze scenes to generate design ideas and determine technical requirements.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Use communication tools (e.g., language, maquettes, pictures, visual storyboard) to convey design ideas (e.g., mood, environment, symbolism).

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Discuss purposes of a paper tech wherein designers meet with the stage manager to discuss and notate costume changes, light and sound transitions and other technical elements.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Interpret a scene through innovative use of various theatrical toolboxes (e.g., director’s, lighting designer’s, scenic designer’s, costume designer’s).

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Use a technical design component (e.g., light, costume, sound, digital technologies) for symbolic purposes as a mode for communicating ideas.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Change the point of view of a scene or dramatic work by amplifying a technical or artistic component (e.g., incorporate audience interaction, replace an actor with an object or technical feature, project digital images on moving actors, use social media conventions in performance).

indicators.label: m
indicators.text: Create a production plan, budget and timeline, and identify roles for a real or imagined (e.g., paper or digital project) production.

indicators.label: n
indicators.text: Use the language of theatre purposefully.

indicators.label: o
indicators.text: Demonstrate willingness to take creative risks, understand that not all ideas will be realized and recognize the value of learning through failure.

indicators.label: p
indicators.text: Reflect on the impact of design decisions on an audience.

indicators.label: q
indicators.text: Examine and experiment with selected traditional world theatre conventions (e.g., design a piece related to a specific theatre arts context).

outcomes.statement: Investigate the history and evolution of technical theatre design practices.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 2: Roots of Theatrical Design (Core) · Suggested Time: 4-6 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 1A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss purposes of technical theatre design (e.g., set, properties, lighting, sound, costume, hair and makeup) including creative functions and practical considerations.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text:
Conduct an inquiry into the history and evolution of technical theatre design, exploring questions such as:
- How do theatre artists and companies create other worlds on stage?
- What lighting was used in spaces and theatres before the advent of electricity?

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Research early technical theatre including conventions (e.g., historic play formats, cultural traditions) and evolution of stage machinery (e.g., engineers such as Adolphe Appia, moveable scenery, flying machines, hydraulic stages, traps).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Examine technical theatre practices from the 1800s (e.g., early special effects, wind machines, waves, elevator stages).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Experiment with elements of technical theatre (e.g., world theatre, Western) using design practices such as thumbnail sketches, renderings and/or models.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Apply ideas, inspired by the history of technical theatre, to own work (e.g., surrealist set, 1940s costumes and hair, Greek or Italian masks, live sound effects).

indicators.label: g
h
indicators.text: Examine the effects of theatrical or playing space locations, architectures and stage configurations (e.g., outdoor, in the round, site- specific, thrust stages, arena stages, black-box, platform, shoebox) on audiences and consider how these diverse contexts impact technical theatre practices.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Explore the role of technical teams when working with collaboratively-devised theatrical performances.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Discuss challenges of early theatrical performances that didn’t have access to technology.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Examine how artistic desires have created technological innovations (e.g., Cirque du Soleil using aerospace engineers to solve artistic problems).

outcomes.statement: Assess performance spaces including those in the school and community.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 3: Performance Spaces (Core) · Suggested Time: 4-6 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Investigate and compare the advantages and disadvantages of various indoor and outdoor performance spaces (e.g., arena/in the round, thrust, proscenium, black box, environmental).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify common areas (e.g., booth, fly gallery, catwalk) and aspects (e.g., curtaining system, grid and lighting system) of a traditional Western theatre performance space.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss Western theatre stage terms (e.g., front of house, apron, arena, backstage, down stage, flexible theatre, in the round, onstage, off stage, proscenium, stage left, stage right, thrust stage, upstage, wings) in the context of a variety of performance spaces.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Differentiate between working parts of a stage and scenery.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Research and examine examples of Canadian Indigenous theatre staging considering performance spaces and technical theatre examples (e.g., use of symbolism and imagery, masks, wardrobe, lighting, sound, music, dance, properties, scenic design).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Research performance spaces of a variety of traditions (e.g., forum theatre, environmental theatre, theatre that moves from venue to venue, First Nations longhouse).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Investigate technical theatre practices of selected world cultures (e.g., Japanese Kabuki makeup, Greek masks, Indonesian gamelan music sound design and shadow puppet theatre).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Identify features of the stage, house and backstage areas of a school, community or professional theatre facility.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Discuss how theatre professionals plan for adaptability to adjust for performance limitations (e.g., space, time parameters).

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Explore opportunities and challenges for a production team related to a selected performance space (e.g., potential interior and exterior performance areas and stages in the school or community) and discuss innovative options.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Recognize the effect the theatre location such as outdoor, theatre in the round, site-specific or historical theatre has on the audience.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Examine how digital technologies could be used in selected performance spaces.

outcomes.statement: Examine and apply basic safety standards in theatre arts work and performance spaces.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 4A: Safety in the Theatre – Rights and Responsibilities (Core) · Suggested Time: 1-3 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss employers’ and employees’ rights and responsibilities pertaining to workplace hazards and how they can work together to prevent workplace hazards in the theatre.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify risks, potential safety hazards and procedures used to ensure safety in theatre environments.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe basic safety procedures used in performance spaces and theatre environments for a variety of tasks such as working with rigging or lighting and working in darkness or at heights.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Examine how safety standards are specific to each area of technical theatre (e.g., electrics, set construction, chemicals, overhead rigging, paints and glues, pyrotechnics, power tools, stage machinery).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Research Occupational Health and Safety regulations that apply to school, community and professional theatre facilities as they pertain to the use of items/features such as steps, risers, ladders, handrails on risers, rigging and traps in stage floor).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Discuss the purpose, scope and application of Safety Data Sheets in the theatre environment.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Research various safety codes (e.g., Canadian Electrical Code) and guidelines used in theatre including their purposes and related procedures.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Investigate safety protocols and guidelines from theatre spaces similar to the school or community playing space.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Co-construct a list of safety rules for general stage use (e.g., wearing close- toed shoes, no drinks on stage, procedures for using machines and stage devices).

outcomes.statement: Investigate artistic and technical approaches used in set design.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 5A: Set Design A (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-8 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 1B

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Examine the function of a set designer.

indicators.label: b
c
indicators.text: Explain and reflect on how sets can create environments for dramatic work (e.g., realistic versus suggested set).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Research and examine the creation of illusions (e.g., projections, transformational set pieces, revolves).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Explore ways that a set design can be rendered using hand skills and digital technologies.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Discuss the importance of researching and honouring the cultural significance of items (e.g., art, furniture, symbols) before incorporating them into set design.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Examine strategies for identifying protocols and processes concerning the representation or use of culturally-sacred items in set design.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Examine the stage and/or set requirements of a selected play or scene and propose ways to create the environment.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Render a simple stage design considering factors such as the design scheme and scale for that space.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Create a basic floor plan using relative scale.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Investigate the purpose (e.g., artistic, functional) of a set model.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Design and create a model (e.g., shoebox), in relative scale, of a real or imagined performance space for one style of set (e.g., realistic, suggested, period, abstract, digitally created).

indicators.label: m
indicators.text: Reflect on personal successes and challenges experienced during design and creation of a real or imagined performance space.

outcomes.statement: Apply methods of categorizing and creating stage properties.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 6A: Stage Properties A (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-10 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Modules 1A and 4A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Define ‘stage properties’ and discuss their purpose in a production.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Brainstorm ways (e.g., hand/action, background, breakaway, consumable/perishable, dress, dummy, rehearsal, set, static, stunt) of categorizing stage properties.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Categorize a variety of stage properties such as food, magazines, weapons, signs, puppets, money, campfires, imaginary creatures and masks.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Create an image bank (e.g., digital, print) to use as inspiration for different categories of properties.

indicators.label: e
f
indicators.text: Design and create a three-dimensional property based on inspiration materials (e.g., photos, drawings, renderings) for a real or imagined production.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Brainstorm and propose solutions to potential problems and situations that might occur in regard to properties.

indicators.label: h
i
indicators.text: Identify reasons why properties must be organized backstage.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Collaborate on a plan to organize the properties for one or more acts of a play that is real or imagined.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Practise safety precautions and procedures when working with stage properties in theatre.

outcomes.statement: Investigate artistic and technical approaches used in set construction.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 7A: Set Construction A (Optional) · Suggested Time: 2-10 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 4B

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Review the roles of the technical director, production manager, scenic artist and other team members as they relate to set construction.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Examine the specific responsibilities of the head carpenter and construction team related to the realization of scenic design concepts.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Investigate how set construction is different from traditional building construction.

indicators.label: d
e
indicators.text: Create an inspirational image bank of theatre set and scenery pieces that demonstrate construction practices considering a variety of factors such as portability, safety, illusion of reality or imagined environments.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Create drawings for the construction of one or more two- or three- dimensional scenery pieces.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Problem-solve ways to identify and simplify construction materials and techniques (e.g., suggestions of walls and windows rather than building the real thing).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Create a two-dimensional (e.g., backdrop, basic 4x8 flat) or three- dimensional (e.g., bush, rock) piece of scenery.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Identify and practise safety precautions (e.g., ensuring platforms meet structural strength standards, using non-combustive materials) required for set construction in a shop and stage setting.

outcomes.statement: Experiment with scenic art materials to create a piece of scenic art.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 8A: Scenic Art A (Optional) · Suggested Time: 2-10 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Modules 1B and 4A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explain the role and specific tasks of scenic artists and painters (e.g., scenic artist interprets the scenic designer’s renderings and paints featured artwork such as wallpaper, backdrops, wood grain, marble or trompe l’oeil whereas a painter lays in colour).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Create an inspirational image bank of designs that demonstrate different functions (e.g., bringing the set designer’s vision to life; creating texture; painting backdrops; using faux to create perspective; creating illusion of space, time and place) of scenic art in theatre.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Create new colours and textures for set pieces by mixing paint.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Experiment with painting techniques (e.g., scumbling, stippling, spattering, lining) to create a variety of surface textures.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Demonstrate the use of perspective when drawing thumbnail sketches for backdrops.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Demonstrate problem-solving strategies when creating illusions.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Propose a scenic art project (e.g., backdrop, throne, flat piece of scenery, the illusion of a three-dimensional object on a two-dimensional surface).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Review safety precautions and practices related to producing scenic art.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Create the proposed scenic art project by hand or with the aid of technology.

outcomes.statement: Investigate artistic and technical approaches used in costume design.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 9A: Costume Design A (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-10 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Modules 1B and 4A

indicators.label: a
b
indicators.text: Describe the role of costume designer in the planning and production stages of theatre.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Create an inspirational image bank of designs that demonstrate different functions of costumes.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Brainstorm different ways to create costumes considering factors such as available resources, skill level, safety, mobility and quick changes.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Examine the process of costume design (e.g., analyzing both text and fabric source material, creating a costume plot, working with director and other designers, creating renderings, draping, construction).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Discuss the role of cultural appreciation in costume design.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Differentiate between costumes and culturally-significant clothing such as regalia, saris and kilts.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Examine strategies for identifying protocols and processes concerning the use of culturally-sacred items in costume design.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Experiment with the design and rendering of costumes (e.g., drawing, making a collage, using interactive apps, sketching silhouettes) for specific characters.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Create preliminary rough sketches for costumes for a specific scene or act, real or imagined.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Identify and practise the principles of theatre safety as they relate to costume design.

outcomes.statement: Apply fundamentals of makeup and hair design in theatre productions.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 10A: Makeup and Hair Design A (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-8 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Modules 1B and 4A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text:
Examine functions of makeup and hair in productions such as:
- creating and communicating information (e.g., personality, socioeconomic background, era, setting, style, situation of role) about the characters;
- supporting visibility of actor; and,
- enhancing, altering or maintaining the appearance of an actor.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Discuss the importance of sanitation and hygiene as they relate to hair and makeup in theatre.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Develop a list of guidelines for safely selecting, applying, removing and storing makeup and hair products.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Create an inspirational image bank of designs that demonstrate selected functions of hair and makeup in theatre.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Research and identify tools and materials used in hair and makeup design and production.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Experiment with basic stage makeup for selected functions.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Demonstrate correct hygiene, sanitation and principles of safety while working with stage hair and makeup tools and products.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Design and create hair and makeup to support a specific character in collaboration with the costume designer.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Recognize the importance of clear communication during theatre production meetings.

outcomes.statement: Investigate artistic and technical approaches used in stage lighting.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 11A: Lighting Design A (Core) · Suggested Time: 4-8 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Modules 1B and 4A

indicators.label: a
b
indicators.text: Examine the basics of colour and light theory (e.g., the colour spectrum, colour and hue, values and intensity of colour, warm and cool colours, distribution of light, movement of light, psychology of colour).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Examine procedures for operating and maintaining lighting equipment.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Demonstrate the operation of a lighting control system (e.g., followspotting).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Demonstrate how to hang, aim, focus and gel lighting instruments.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Identify and practise safety precautions and procedures for stage lighting.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Create an inspirational image bank of designs that demonstrate selected functions of lighting in theatre.

outcomes.statement: Investigate artistic and technical approaches used in sound design.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 12A: Sound Design A (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-8 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Modules 1B and 4A

indicators.label: a
b
indicators.text: Experiment with basic recording and playback sound systems, including analog and digital systems, and explore controllable properties such as pitch, volume, quality, direction and duration.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Research and explore fundamentals of stage sound and video in theatre.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Create and find sources for sound effects.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss and examine ways of organizing sound (e.g., plot, cue sheets) for stage productions or events.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Follow a sound script.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Identify and practise safety precautions and procedures when working with stage sound and video.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Create an inspirational sound bank of designs that demonstrate selected functions of sound in theatre.

outcomes.statement: Apply technical skills to create stage projections that incorporate projection design.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 13: Projection Design and Technologies (Optional) · Suggested Time: 2-8 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Modules 1B and 4A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Investigate the functions of projection design and use of projection systems and technologies.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Discuss projection design processes (e.g., researching, storyboarding, acquiring images or footage, editing, installing, controlling).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explore ways that projections (e.g., front versus rear, slideshow software, animation and other video, shadow play) can be created and used in theatre.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Investigate different ways to create projections considering technical specifications and factors such as the projectors’ lumens, throw distance, throw ratio, physics of light, intensity of light and direction.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Experiment with the creation and refinement of projections (e.g., replacing constructed set design items with still images, comparing presentation software, trying short-throw lens, projecting moving images, adjusting theater lighting, avoiding unwanted shadows, playing with fades and transitions).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Experiment with different types of projection screens (e.g., white screens versus black screens versus gray, blank walls, painted portable plywood screen, painter’s plastic stretched on a frame, existing cyclorama, Screen Goo painted surfaces, fabric screens, rear-projection screen or frosted shower curtains) and adjust stage lighting to compare results (e.g., black screens transmit less light than white but have more contrast and resist unwanted ambient light).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Create an inspirational ideas bank of designs that use projections for various purposes.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Identify and practise safety precautions and procedures when working with projection equipment.

indicators.text: Function as a responsible and useful crew member in a stage production applying theatre arts research, knowledge and practical skills.

indicators.text: Review the roles and responsibilities of various department heads, co- ordinators and team members to determine how one might provide support in a specific role or department.

Research answers to questions related to the geography of the destination, such as:

evidence.observation: The curriculum document groups its outcomes under 3 headings: “Grade Ten: Examining the Canadian context for Treaties”, “Grade Eleven: Assessing Treaty Making from a Global Perspective”, “Grade Twelve: Applying Treaty Understandings to One’s Life”.

If you are trying to access a curriculum, it might have been renewed. Please use the menu above to search for the updated version.” Its curriculum document link (https://curriculum.gov.sk.ca/CurriculumFile?id=481) answers the same “Page Not Found” page; the outcomes are taken from the curriculum document the site's menus link (https://www.edonline.sk.ca/bbcswebdav/xid-8784654_1); see `document`.

units.name: Grade Eleven: Assessing Treaty Making from a Global Perspective

items.text: Examine how Canada’s process of treaty making could be applied to situations in other parts of the world where Indigenous people have struggled to have rights recognized.
Apply the principles of Canadian treaty making as a means for resolving conflict and represent it (e.g. dramatization, visual, dance, oral representation, multi media presentation).
Investigate how the United Nations addresses issues regarding the self-determination of Indigenous peoples.
Analyze how the unfulfilled aspects of treaties, with international indigenous people, have resulted in inequities.
Analyze international examples of treaties involving indigenous peoples that have resulted in inequities.
Research how the Indian Act and its implementation differ in practice from First Nation governance structures.
Explore legal, political, ethical, and social impacts within Canada where Treaties do not exist.
Evaluate specific treaties that have been, or currently are, in place globally to determine their effectiveness.
Conduct an inventory of the various treaties that currently exist.
Assess the various motives for entering into treaty.
Construct a recommendation as to the effectiveness of treaty as a means for addressing conflict (e.g., a motion, passing of a law).
Research UN resolutions and initiatives in relation to self-determination of indigenous peoples.
Analyze the impact Canadian treaties could have on resolving global conflict.
Assess Canadian treaty making processes and compare to treaty processes from around the world.
Assess the leadership role Canada plays internationally in treaty making.

notes: Treaty Education is organised by grade (10, 11, 12), not by course level, and is meant to be taught within other subjects. `level` gives the matching course level (Grade 10 = 10-level, 11 = 20-level, 12 = 30-level) only so the course can sit beside the others.
Outcome codes are printed with a superscript goal number (TR¹, SI², HC³, TPP⁴, per the page's KEY); the superscript is kept in `superscript`, and `code` is the code as the Ministry CSV lists it.

The site's outcomes page for Treaty Education (https://curriculum.gov.sk.ca/CurriculumOutcomeContent?id=481) and its curriculum document link (https://curriculum.gov.sk.ca/CurriculumFile?id=481) both answer the site's “Page Not Found” page (checked 2026-11-21).

outcomes.statement: Investigate art works from around the world that address the human rights of Indigenous and various cultures.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explore and describe connections between art works that express social commentary concerning peoples from around the world (e.g., art works that comment on issues such as Indigenous health, racism, self-determination, environmental degradation).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Conduct an inquiry into how art has helped to sustain the cultures of Saskatchewan First Nations and Métis and other Indigenous peoples of the world.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Research and discuss art works that comment on the effects of colonization in Saskatchewan and around the world.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Conduct an overview of treaties (e.g., treaty education outcome HC11 - evaluate specific treaties that have been, or currently are, in place globally to determine their effectiveness; and, outcome SI11 - analyze how the unfulfilled aspects of treaties, with international indigenous people, have resulted in inequities) and related human rights issues globally (e.g., Maori, Mapoon, South American, South Africa), and examine the work of Indigenous artists from those regions.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Examine the work of artists whose art communicates personal experiences with human rights issues (e.g., newcomer artists).

outcomes.statement: Investigate how artists from around the world incorporate and manipulate media, form and content in interdisciplinary work.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Research a variety of sources (e.g., websites, galleries, communication media) to observe how artists incorporate and manipulate media, form and content in interdisciplinary work.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Respond to artistic and interactive presentations that utilize creative technologies (e.g., film and photo documentaries, movement-activated sculptures, interactive installations, performance art).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Create art works and corresponding documentation to demonstrate an artistic technique and/or materials used in a work of art from a specific time in history (e.g., 1930s linocuts, Greek clay coiling, Renaissance egg tempera painting).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Examine aspects of culture and history to determine how artists have impacted art historical and social norms and constructs (e.g., participatory arts expressions, social constructs of gender).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Examine the work of artists who incorporate and infuse traditional art forms with contemporary work (e.g., street art, mixed media assemblages, traditional beading patterns used in large scale paintings, historical references in contemporary clothing designs, combining text and images).

outcomes.statement: 3 Investigate opportunities in arts communities and visual art-related practices and careers in Saskatchewan, Canada and the world.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Research formal and informal education opportunities and career paths taken by various local, Canadian and international visual artists (e.g., mentorships, professional associations, community workshops, Indigenous art-making and teaching practices, post-secondary education opportunities).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Investigate various funding (e.g., scholarships) and grant opportunities for continuing visual art practice including professional development for emerging and professional artists.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explore job shadowing, mentorship and collaborative project opportunities in own communities.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Interview a prominent artist about his/her education and career path.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Examine how visual art, and the other arts, contribute to personal and social wellbeing in communities.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Investigate educational qualifications required to pursue various post-secondary pathways and career options.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Examine roles, responsibilities and personal and professional qualities needed to continue developing an ongoing visual art practice.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Investigate artist collectives, alternative gallery environments, artist run centers, or student run art pop-up center, and consider opportunities to volunteer in own community.

outcomes.statement: Impovising in a jazz style, exploring understanding of applicable jazz theory.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss understanding of jazz style and analyze musical events within a solo or composition(e.g. introduction, shout chorus, form, dynamics, pitches, changes, articulation).

indicators.label: b
c
d
e
indicators.text: Demonstrate improvement and growth in the presentation and construction of improvised solos in a performance setting.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Take personal and musical risks by trying new ways to express oneself in the jazz idiom, using new ideas, new concepts and a variety of styles.

outcomes.statement: Integrate, with assistance as necessary, the understanding of the muscial text into a personal musical performance.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Prepare, rehearse and perform music in jazz style in solo, small group and/or large ensemble settings.

indicators.label: b
c
indicators.text: Experiment with text through creating original text to pre-existing melodies and improvisations (vocalese)

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Develop knowledge of conventions regarding jazz articulation and use those conventions in performance.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Begin to use jazz vocabulary and use this vocabulary to describe personal musical practise, learning, theory and performance (see Jazz Glossary).

outcomes.statement: Identify the elements of music and apply these to create a musical product.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Employ in performance the knowledge of standard notation conventions (e.g., note durations up to eighth notes, repeats, codas, D.S.s and dynamic markings). Identify jazz conventions that differ from traditional classical notation (e.g., falls, glisses, slides, inflection marks and hats).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Sing a variety of vocal jazz styles (e.g., swing, funk, ballad) accompanied and a cappella.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explore the understanding of the relationship of form and text in music, particularly blues and ABA, AABA song forms.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: With assistance, design, implement and evaluate a plan to improve individual performance and to enhance the knowledge and uderstanding of vocal jazz. As part of this process of improvement, include recording and listening back to performances, practices and/or rehearsals.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify different elements of music such as articulation, rhythm, beat, metre, time placement and tone that help create a jazz style and apply this knowledge while music making.

outcomes.statement: Explore individual vocal techniques and apply these to create or show a musical product.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Demonstrate a vocal tone appropriate to the style and personal development.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Demonstrate the connection betrween the breath and the voice.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Demonstrate the key concepts related to singing expressively (e.g., work painting, phrasing, motion and dynamics). Show the knowledge of these concepts through singing.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Demonstrate the knowledge of good microphone techniques in rehearsals and performance of music.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Sing a one octave chromatic scale, scending and descending, unaccompanied.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Sing one octave major, harmonic minor and blues scales, ascending and descending, unaccompanied.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Sing the chord tones of major and minor triads, dominant and major 7ths, and scale triads.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Sing a jazz standard (with recorded or live acompaniment) exploring scat singin and other appropriate jazz stylings.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Sight-read a melodic line written in stepwise motions

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Compare and contrast vocal jazz style to other vocal styles.

outcomes.statement: Develop skills and abilities required to listen and respond as a vocal jazz performer when singing jazz.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Respond to qualities of personal tone such as pitch, dynamics, style, colour, blend, rhythm, time, and consistent vowel use.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Respond to the rest of the ensemble (e.g., its tone, colour, pitch, dynamics, style, rhythm, time, balance, consistent vowel use and blend).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Immediately respond to the ensemble's response (e.g., When singing, does the student match and change vowel sounds and shapes to match the group?).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Respond to the conductor/leader, including gestures, cues, tempo, expressions and body language.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Listen to the acoustic properties of the performing space, including the sound, tone, loudness, and reverb of the room and adjust singing and microphone technique accordingly.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: React to the audience, their presence (or nor), body language, expressions and reaction to the music (e.g., applause, cheering, being asked to sing louder or quieter).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Know the history, culture, style, form and tempo of the music being performed and respond to the music by reading it and/or performing the notes and/or changes appropriately

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Recall previous experiences and knowledge (in music and in life) and integrate these into solo group vocal jazz performances.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Know any special emotional context that may apply to the music, generate the appropriate emotional feeling or energy and/or synchronize the personal emotional state of the performer with the emotional context of the music being performed.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Know, predict and/or anticipate what is next or might bve next in the music and prepare for that while performing in the moment of the music.

outcomes.statement: Develop skills and abilities necessary to listen to jazz as a jazz performer when not personally performing the music.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Listen to jazz music and with assistance analyze form, tone, style, era, dynamics, articulation, time signature, characteristic rhythms, time, balance, blend, key, monde and/or pitch.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text:
Analyze the development of the jazz music(melody, arrangement, changes, or improvisation) as a whole or in smaller sections.
;

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Analyze the characteristic sounds, licks, tone and other elements of well-known singers and/or groups. Identify these singers and/or groups. Identify these singers and/or groups on recordings aurally, only by listening to the characteristic sounds or ideas presented in the music.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Analyze and reflect on just one voice or instrument from the beginning to the end of a musical selection (e.g., Does the singer or player perform the same way all the way through? How was it different or the same? What did he/she sing or play that the student also might be able to sing or play?)

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Listen to music analyzing and reflecting on the melody, other voices, bass line, drums and percussion, background lines, background vocals, roots and chord progression and sing with the recording.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Discuss the history, cultural heritage and effect of current events as these apply to the musical selection.

outcomes.statement: Develop the skills and abilities to analyze vocal jazz music in real time while making or listening to the music.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Individually and in groups identify, experiment with, and purposefully use strategies to solve different challenges related to music making.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify the time signatures on first hearing a piece of music, including 6/8, in addition to simpler duple time signatures. Demonstrate the patters of strong and weak beats that are identified with the time signatures

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Use strategies to identify the types of scales being used (pentatonic, blues, major, etc.) in music performed and/or listened to.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Develp strategies for hearing 2 and 4 on first hearing a piece of music in an appropriate time signature.

outcomes.statement: Listen to performances of vocal jazz music and individually or with assistance develop and apply critical criteria to use in critical exaluation of one's own work and other's work.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Listen to the music of the great jazz and vocal jazz performers.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Generate criteria of excellence through listening to the music of the great performers (e.g., What is it that makes the music great? what do the great performers do that the student or student's ensemble does no do?)

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: With assistance or in groups, design and implement a plan for improvement (personal and ensemble) based on the criteria generated from listening to the great performers.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: When listening to a musical selection, as a group develop the ability to describe and classify the music using appropriate jazz language (e.g., style, period, compose, culture and performer).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Refine the skills and components of listening actively, continue to develop these listening skill and recognize that listening contributes to the authenticity of performances.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Recognize and discuss the value of original thought, technical proficiency, place, era and other concepts in the music of the great jazz performers.

outcomes.statement: Demonstrate the knowledge and implementation of the skills, techniques and attitudes necessary for successful ensemble performace.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Know the role of each of the parts within the student's ensemble by demonstrating the ability to perform those specific tasks that are particular to the vocal part or instrument that the student sings or plays in the ensemble (e.g., bass part in the choir, comping for guitar and piano, walking lines for the bass, solo parts in the choir and position in a section).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Attend to melodic phrasing, rhythmic accuracy and articulation in perparation and performance of vocal jazz.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Sing in tune with good balance and tone and be aware of the qualities of the student's own voice (e.g., range, where the break in the student's voice is).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Develop leadership as a performer by offering help, ideas and guideance to other performers during rehearsals and sectionals.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Demonstrate a professional attitude towards conduct, focus and communication skills in rehearsal, preparation of materials and presentation of products.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Employ the learned characteristics of different styles, eras, etc. to the performance of the student's music.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explore understanding of PA systems including set up, tone and level settings for microphones, and so on.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Show respect for the personal work of self and others through appropriate critique.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Critically examine and assess the student's individual work and personal contributions to group projects/performances, with assistance as necessary.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Be accepting ofappropriate critiques from others, and work towards implementing the solutions to those critiques.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: With assistance as necessary, demonstrate and record technical development, and from that, develop strategies to improve.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Know the value of individual practice, know how to practive, conduct an ongoing evaluation of the student's personal practice skills, and implement a plan for improvement.

outcomes.statement: Develop knowledge of the different eras, genres, styles and feels of vocal jazz through listening to and.or performing the representative music.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Individually and in groups, listen to recording of vocal jazz, develop a list or understanding of the basic characteristics of different jazz styles, genres, periods and place and implement that knowledge into practice and performance.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Individually and as a group listen to recordings of vocal jazz and catagorize the music into styles, genres, periods and/or place.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explore aspects of vocal jazz such as history, performers, styles and eras through a variety of media, with a focus on Canadian or Saskatchewan jazz artists.

outcomes.statement: Explore jazz music and its performers and educators and their influence in the world.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Investigate some of the challenges that vocal jazz artists with African America, First Nations, and/or mixed race heritage may have had in their daily lives, and compare to the situations faced by many groups of people today.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Research how vocal jazz artists may raise or have raised awareness of local, national and international issues (e.g., Billie Holiday singing "Strange Fruit" or Manhattan Transfer singing "Aqua").

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss the influence of jazz (and other musics) on contemporary First Nations music.

outcomes.statement: Evaluate the degree of influence that vocal jazz has had on other types of music with an emphasis on the music of Canada and Saskatchewan, and assess possible careers in vocal jazz and music

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify influential vocal ensembles, investigate why these performers are so influential and listen to their music. Give special attention to performers from Saskatchewan and Canada

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Investigate the relationship between instrumental and vocal jazz, with particular emphasis on vocal performers who "imitate" insturmental sounds (e.g., Bobby McFerrin, Mark Murphy, Giacommo Gates, Louis Armstrong, Ella Fitzgerald).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe how Canadian and international copyright laws affect the lives of those who work in the jazz field.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Research career pathways in vocal jazz and music in general.

outcomes.statement: Work safely with properly maintained safety equipment in an organized environment.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Express knowledge of safe handling of materials according to WHMIS, using materials safety data sheets (MSDS).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Research and discuss Occupational Health and Safety regulations which apply to the welding industry.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Recognize and apply safe and fair work practices including freedom from violence and harassment.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Complete an assessment of all safety and welding equipment and, in consultation with the instructor, perform maintenance to repair or replace defective or worn parts.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Demonstrate the proper method for cleaning weld-spattered tools.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Assess and report any potential faults with electrical cords and receptacles.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Repair or replace welding-distorted surfaces on benches or table tops in consultation with the instructor.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Demonstrate the proper techniques to remove and replace saw blades.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify potential maintenance issues with hand and power tools and consult with the instructor to determine a solution.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Complete bevel cuts on 3⁄8” mild steel.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Cut holes and circles on 3⁄8” mild steel.

outcomes.statement: Effectively use oxy-acetylene equipment to increase the quality of the specified welds.

indicators.text: Perform and analyze a variety of specified welds, including butt weld, edge weld, and lines of fusion.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Compare and chart personal progress to identify increasing skill.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Assess personal technique and document results in consultation with the instructor.

outcomes.statement: Demonstrate increasing proficiency in oxy-acetylene welding skills.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 11B: Oxy-acetylene Welding Practice (Core) · Suggested Time: 20-25 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 10

indicators.text: Perform a butt weld using filler rod, in the flat position, on gauge mild steel ensuring 100% penetration.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Perform a butt weld using filler rod, in the vertical position, on gauge mild steel.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Perform a lap weld using filler rod, in the flat position, on gauge mild steel; overlap by half.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Assess personal technique and document results in consultation with the instructor.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and describe safety considerations for appropriate use of plasma arc cutting equipment.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Correctly use plasma arc cutting equipment to perform various cuts specified by the instructor.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Verify the correct pressure settings and techniques to safely cut ferrous and non-ferrous metals of given thicknesses.

indicators.text: Perform a lap weld on ¼” mild steel using 7014, 7018, and 6010 electrodes.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Perform an outside corner weld (horizontal and vertical fillet on ¼” mild steel) using 7018 electrode.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Perform horizontal fillets (¼” and 3⁄8” multi-pass on ¼” mild steel) using 7014, 7018, and 7024 electrodes.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Perform a butt weld flat (single pass; 6010 electrode; 75% penetration on ¼” mild steel).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Perform a 3⁄8” vee butt flat (introductory only; 6010 root, 7018 fill and cap).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Compare and chart personal progress to identify increasing skill.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Assess personal technique and results in consultation with the instructor.

outcomes.statement: Construct an introductory assigned or approved arc welding project.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 21A: Introductory Project (Optional) · Suggested Time: 15-20 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 19

indicators.label: a
indicators.text:
Utilize the following guidelines to complete a project:
- Generate different project ideas
- Plan and manage the project including assessment criteria in consultation with the instructor
- Plan and use drawings with appropriate symbols
- Set a procedural sequence
- Prepare a material list and cost estimate
- Create a timeline
- Determine fabrication techniques
- Cut material and set up in the proper sequence
- Complete each part as specified
- Interpret and follow directions
- Adhere to timelines
- Work cooperatively
- Follow all safety requirements
- Follow all handling and storing procedures
- Fulfill cleanup and tool maintenance responsibilities
- Present the completed project and complete a self-assessment based on the criteria for the project.

outcomes.statement: Demonstrate and explain the importance of employing the correct start-up and shutdown procedures for GMAW equipment.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Review personal protective equipment (PPE) standards for usage.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Adjust the machine for appropriate wire speed, voltage, and amperage.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Turn on shielding gas and describe the reading on the flow meter.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Demonstrate the correct start-up and shut-down procedures, including checking and cleaning up the work station.

indicators.text: Demonstrate proper use of GMAW equipment assembly including disassembly of welding gun, adjustment of flow meter, and wire selection and installation.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Safely operate hand tools, power hand tools, and power equipment.

outcomes.statement: Develop increasing skill using GMAW equipment.

indicators.text: Perform a horizontal fillet on 14 gauge steel.

indicators.label: b

indicators.text: Perform horizontal fillets (¼” and 3⁄8” multi-pass on ¼” mild steel; short circuit transfer).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Perform horizontal fillets (¼” and 3⁄8” multi-pass on ¼” mild steel; spray transfer).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Compare and chart personal progress to identify increasing skill.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Assess personal technique and results in consultation with the instructor.

outcomes.statement: Recognize how school-based skills development will be used to meet workplace expectations.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 31A: Work Study Preparation (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Intermediate, Advanced · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Obtain a list of roles and responsibilities of the workplace.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Brainstorm a list of factors which may affect workplace performance.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss effective and positive verbal and non-verbal communication.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Develop a résumé which can be forwarded to a potential employer.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Practise effective interview techniques based on established guidelines including the greeting, the exchange, and the parting.

outcomes.statement: Gain experience in the world of work to make more informed choices about careers by expanding the career research and exploration beyond the classroom.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Develop an awareness of career and opportunities in Saskatchewan and possibly other provinces.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Gain an opportunity for the development of entry level workplace skills that may lead to sustainable employment.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Establish standards of work performance acceptable to the student and employer.

indicators.text: Demonstrate the required skills and perform the duties expected by the employer.

indicators.text: Identify and report on essential skills and employability skills as they relate to a work environment.

Prepare and present a report on the work study experience including aspects such as:

- Dress code and personal protective equipment (PPE)

- Problem solving
- Communication.

outcomes.statement: Practise the “Leave No Trace” principles on outdoor excursions.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 2B: Leave No Trace - Application (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 2A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss the importance of planning and preparing in advance of excursions, including to ensure safety and minimize resource damage.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Compare the effects on the land of camping and traveling on and off durable surfaces.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text:
Demonstrate respect for the natural setting by:
- minimizing campsite alterations;
- avoiding damage to trees and plants; and,
- leaving natural objects where they are found.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text:
Explore options for proper disposal of human waste outdoors, such as:
- digging catholes;
- portable toilets; and,
- packing out waste (e.g., toilet paper and feminine hygiene products).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Investigate minimal impact alternatives to cooking over a fire (e.g., envirostove, fire box and gas stove).

indicators.label: f
g
indicators.text: Demonstrate respect for wildlife by keeping distance and storing food securely.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Discuss options for dealing with food waste (e.g., completely burning and packing out).

outcomes.statement: Explore basic first aid skills used to treat minor to severe injuries.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 3B: Wilderness Safety - First Aid (Optional) · Suggested Time: 4-20 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 3A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explain the terms “first aid,” “first aider” and “Good Samaritan law.”

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe how to ensure the safety of the person providing first aid (e.g., gloves and scan the area).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify injuries common to an activity (e.g., head injuries while cycling) and steps taken to prevent them (e.g., wearing a helmet).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Define primary and secondary surveys in first aid.

indicators.label: e
f
indicators.text: Explain the additional risks of emergency situations that occur in the wilderness, such as lack of proximity to treatment and lack of sterilization.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Compare the items appropriate to include in a personal first aid kit (e.g., band-aids, personal medications and sunscreen) and a group first aid kit (e.g., medical gloves, gauze and bandages).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explore opportunities for, and benefits of, being certified in first aid.

outcomes.statement: Participate in a variety of outdoor activities.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 4: Outdoor Activities (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-20 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explain the role of physical conditioning in safe and comfortable outdoor experiences.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Compare nutritional and hydration requirements when participating in light to heavy exercise.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Display basic swimming skills such as floating, treading water and kicking and stroking.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explain the “Swim to Survive” standard of the Life Saving Society.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Demonstrate basic canoe safety and rescue skills, such as getting in and out of a canoe, carrying a canoe, t-rescues and effective throw bag technique.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Practise canoe strokes (e.g., forward and reverse, draw, pry, j-stroke or stern rudder, sweep and brace) for different purposes.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Exhibit use of basic cycling techniques such as hand signals, braking safely and gear shifting to accommodate for changes in incline.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Apply hiking skills (e.g., pacing, adjusting pack, stretching and resting) when hiking in various terrains, such as urban and wilderness treks.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Demonstrate safe techniques in climbing activities (e.g., high ropes and wall climbing).

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Experiment with different snowshoe skills (e.g., step and kick turns, striding, stamping and edging).

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Practise cross-country ski techniques (e.g., diagonal stride on flat ground, herringbone uphill and snowplough downhill) for different purposes.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Engage in outdoor evening activities such as star gazing, identifying moon phases and night hiking.

outcomes.statement: Apply navigational skills in a variety of situations.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 5B: Navigation (Optional) · Suggested Time: 4-10 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 5A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Orient and interpret a map using the legend and topographical lines of elevation.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain declination and its considerations for compass navigation.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Calculate declination to travel on a bearing using a compass.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Navigate a route using a compass and map.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Compare the benefits of using a map and compass or a Global Positioning System (GPS) to navigate in different situations.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explore how common hand-held technology such as cell phones can be used as a navigational tool.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explain the purpose of waypoints when using a GPS.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Plan a route for others to follow using waypoints.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Compare the function and use of a GPS and Geographical Information Systems (GIS).

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Explore the uses of a GIS application such as Sask Interactive Mapping.

outcomes.statement: Apply knot-tying skills in a variety of situations.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 6B: Advanced Ropes and Knots Skills (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-8 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 6A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss the importance of strong cordage and efficient knot skills in Indigenous ways of living off the land.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Apply knot-tying skills to related outdoor skills, such as tying up tarp shelters, tying fishing knots (e.g., fisherman's knot and palomar knot) and tying nets.

indicators.label: c
d
indicators.text: Explain the factors to consider in rope making (e.g., strength and breaking point).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Investigate the usefulness of paracord in bushcraft survival.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Experiment with the application of paracord in paracord crafts (e.g., lanyards and bracelets).

outcomes.statement: Practise a variety of sustainable shelter-building techniques.
